nodes.label: Model Training Agentic Workflow
nodes.description:
Deliver an end-to-end agentic workflow for scaffolding, executing, and surfacing results from ML training jobs. Triggered by a single `/train` command, the workflow copies the appropriate template, merges user-supplied config overrides, optionally executes training via a managed MCP subprocess or emits a `start.sh` for manual execution, and surfaces structured results (terminal, markdown, JSON, and type-specific HTML dashboard) on completion.

All execution behaviours are opt-in and controlled via a `workflow:` block in `config.yaml` and/or CLI flags.

nodes.label: /train Skill — Job Scaffolding
nodes.description: As a developer, I want `/train new <type> <job-name>` to scaffold a ready-to-use job directory from the appropriate template so that I don't manually copy templates or wire config every time I start a training job.

nodes.label: workflow: Config Block in Training Templates
nodes.description: As a developer, I want all three template `config.yaml` files to ship with a fully documented `workflow:` block so that execution behaviour is explicit, self-documenting, and configurable out of the box without needing to read external docs.

nodes.label: training_runner MCP Tool
nodes.description: As a developer, I want an MCP tool that runs a training job as a managed subprocess so that the agent can execute, monitor, and stream training output within the session without leaving the workflow context.

nodes.label: start.sh Generation
nodes.description: As a developer, I want a `start.sh` script emitted in the job directory when `generate_start_sh: true` so that I can run training manually outside the agent session and still benefit from result surfacing on completion.

nodes.label: Result Surfacing
nodes.description: As a developer, I want training results parsed and surfaced in four formats automatically after training completes so that I can immediately review outcomes without manually digging through output files.

nodes.label: Training Skill Assets & Standardized Templates
nodes.description: As a developer using the `/train` skill, I want each model training type (classifiers, transformers, nlp) to ship with a self-contained set of standardized assets — minimal but correctly structured stub data, a type-specific `validate.py`, a smoke-testable `train.py`, and a version-stamped `config.yaml` — so that a scaffolded job can be immediately verified and run without any manual setup.

nodes.label: AI Engineer Agent
nodes.description: As a user setting up or training an AI model, I want a dedicated `ai_engineer` agent that handles the deep technical work — so that I don't need to understand LLM/ML internals directly. The `scrum-master` acts as a mediator between me and the `ai_engineer`: translating technical questions and proposals into plain language for me, and converting my responses back into precise technical terms for the engineer.

nodes.label: Interactive Train Wizard
nodes.description: As a user setting up a new training job, I want to run `train new --interactive` and be guided through the critical configuration decisions — so that I don't have to manually edit `config.yaml` after scaffolding.

nodes.label: Agent Conversation Guardrails
nodes.description: Equip the Jenga agent system with conversation-awareness guardrails that detect when a user is diverging from the primary topic of a session. When divergence is detected, the agent surfaces a structured choice: capture the diverging topic as a `/todo` (and continue the primary discussion) or capture the primary topic as a `/todo` (and pivot to the diverging subject). Both paths preserve context and continuity without losing either thread.

nodes.label: Subject Divergence Detection
nodes.description: As a user working through a focused session, I want the agent to notice when I'm drifting into a new subject and offer me a structured way to capture either thread as a `/todo` — so that no context is lost and I can consciously choose which topic to continue.

nodes.label: /spinoff Skill
nodes.description: As a user mid-conversation, I want to invoke `/spinoff` to formally declare a diverging topic — so that the agent captures it as a structured `/todo` with context gathered so far, and we can consciously continue one thread without losing the other.

nodes.label: Parallel Workflow Orchestration
nodes.description: Extend the Jenga skill system with orchestration capabilities that allow multiple implementation tasks to be executed in parallel by sub-agents. The orchestrator skill (`/dooo`) wraps `/do` with a feedback loop that returns to the scrum board after each implementation is kicked off, identifies tasks that can safely run in parallel with the already-running ones, and presents them to the user so they can choose to fan out further or call it done.

nodes.label: Dataset Conversion Skill (/convert)
nodes.description:
Deliver a standalone `/convert` skill that normalises dataset files into CSV format for consumption by ML training jobs. The skill auto-detects the input format by file extension, flattens nested structures using dot-notation, and passes through files that are already CSV without modification.

The skill operates as a pre-processing step in the `/train` workflow — invoked automatically by the interactive train wizard when a non-CSV data file is provided — and can also be used standalone for general data preparation.

nodes.label: Core /convert Skill
nodes.description: As a user preparing data for a training job, I want to run `/convert` on a JSON, JSONL, or YAML dataset file and get back a clean CSV — so that I can feed it directly into any `/train` job without manual preprocessing.

nodes.label: Wire /convert into /train Interactive Wizard
nodes.description: As a user running the interactive train wizard, I want non-CSV data files to be automatically converted to CSV — so that I don't have to manually run `/convert` before setting up my job.

nodes.label: Agent Dashboard — API Layer
nodes.description: Make jenga run as a headless local HTTP/JSON server that exposes scrum board state, project history, and architecture metadata through a well-designed, integration-friendly REST API. MCP bindings are supported as a thin optional layer on top. The server is architecturally independent of any specific consumer — the dashboard webapp, CLI tools, and future third-party integrations all connect to it the same way.

nodes.label: API Contract & Design Principles
nodes.description: As a developer building integrations on top of jenga, I want a clearly documented API contract so that I can build consumers confidently without relying on implementation details.

nodes.label: Server Bootstrap & Routing
nodes.description: As a developer, I want the jenga API server to start cleanly with a structured router and a health endpoint so that consumers can verify connectivity before making data requests.

nodes.label: Board Endpoints
nodes.description: As a dashboard consumer, I want API endpoints that return the full scrum board parsed from local markdown files so that I can render epics, stories, and tasks without reading files directly.

nodes.label: History Endpoints
nodes.description: As a dashboard consumer, I want an endpoint that returns a combined project history of git commits and local rapport/session summaries so that I can display a unified timeline without reading raw files.

nodes.label: Architecture Endpoints
nodes.description: As a dashboard consumer, I want an endpoint that returns the project's tech stack and dependency versions parsed from local config files so that I can display an up-to-date architecture overview.

nodes.label: Service Directory Relocation
nodes.description: As a developer working across E05–E09, I want the API and dashboard services relocated to a canonical path inside `project/app/` so that all future stories build on a consistent, well-structured directory layout.

nodes.label: Agent Dashboard — Board Tab
nodes.description: Deliver a read-only visual board in the dashboard webapp that displays epics, stories, and tasks in a Jira-like layout. The webapp is architecturally independent of the API server — it connects via a configurable `API_BASE_URL` and can be served by jenga or run standalone against any compatible API.

nodes.label: App Shell & API Client
nodes.description: As a developer, I want the web app scaffolded with a configurable API base URL and tab routing so that the dashboard can connect to any running jenga API server and navigate between tabs.

nodes.label: Board View
nodes.description: As a user, I want to see my scrum board rendered visually in the dashboard so that I can review epics, stories, and tasks at a glance without reading markdown files.

nodes.label: [SPIKE] Editable Board
nodes.description: Research and document how inline board editing (status changes, reordering, field updates) could be implemented on top of the existing read-only board. No code is produced — output is a design note.

nodes.label: Collapsible Epic → Story → Task Tree
nodes.description: As a user viewing the dashboard's Board tab, I want epics and stories to be collapsible/expandable, defaulting to fully collapsed, so that I can scan a large board without every task rendering at once.

nodes.label: Kanban-Style Status Columns for Board View
nodes.description: As a user viewing the dashboard's Board tab, I want epics/stories/tasks laid out as a kanban board with one column per status, so I can see at a glance what's pending, active, stuck, or shipped without scanning a flat list.

nodes.label: Filter Board by Status
nodes.description: As a user viewing the dashboard's Board tab, I want to filter the board by one or more statuses at once, so I can narrow the view down to just the items I care about (e.g. only `Blocked` and `Failed` items) without scanning the whole tree.

nodes.label: Agent Dashboard — History Tab
nodes.description: Display a chronological project history view combining git commit log and session rapport/markdown summaries sourced entirely from local files. No GitHub API or external network calls.

nodes.label: History View
nodes.description: As a user, I want to see a unified project timeline in the dashboard combining git commits and session rapport summaries so that I can understand what has happened in the project over time.

nodes.label: Entry Detail Panel
nodes.description: As a user, I want to click a history entry and see its full detail so that I can read a complete commit message or rapport without leaving the dashboard.

nodes.label: Agent Dashboard — Architecture Tab
nodes.description: Provide a visual overview of the project's tech stack and dependency versions, parsed from local project config files. No live registry lookups. A spike explores what a Security section could contain in a future iteration.

nodes.label: Architecture View
nodes.description: As a user, I want to see my project's tech stack and dependency versions displayed in the dashboard so that I have a quick reference for what the project is built with.

nodes.label: [SPIKE] Security Section
nodes.description: Research and document what a Security section in the Architecture tab could contain. No code is produced — output is a design note.

nodes.label: SAD Map in Architecture View
nodes.description: As a user, I want to see a visual diagram of the project's services and components — and how they connect — in the Architecture tab, so I can quickly understand the system's structure at a glance.

nodes.label: SAD Map Interactivity
nodes.description: As a user, I want to click nodes on the SAD map to focus on a specific item and its direct connections, so I can explore the architecture diagram without being overwhelmed by the full graph.

nodes.label: Source Architecture Map from graph.json
nodes.description: As a user, I want the Architecture tab's SAD map to be rendered from the knowledge graph rather than parsed live from board markdown, so that the dashboard reflects the same architecture data model the rest of the project uses instead of duplicating its own board-parsing logic.

nodes.label: Agent Dashboard — CLI Interface (PoC)
nodes.description: Deliver a minimal proof-of-concept CLI interface for starting the jenga API server and opening the dashboard from the terminal. This epic is intentionally thin — it validates the end-to-end flow without building a full terminal emulator. Implemented last, after the API layer and webapp are stable.

nodes.label: `jenga dashboard start` Command
nodes.description: As a user, I want to start the jenga API server (and optionally serve the web app) with a single CLI command so that I can get the dashboard running without manual setup.

nodes.label: `jenga dashboard open` Command
nodes.description: As a user, I want a CLI command that opens the dashboard in my default browser so that I don't have to remember the URL or keep a terminal window in focus.

nodes.label: Script Infrastructure & Skill Refactor
nodes.description: Replace ad-hoc `todo.md` file operations and board-path guessing scattered across skill instructions with two canonical shell scripts — `todo_manager.sh` and `board_resolver.sh` — and update all affected skills to call them. Introduce a structured handoff template (owned by `/todo`) so any skill invoking `/todo` with pre-collected context can skip repeated Q&A. Add a session-end safety net that automatically cleans up effectively-empty `todo.md` files.

nodes.label: `scripts/todo_manager.sh`
nodes.description: As a skill or script author, I want a single canonical shell script that owns all `todo.md` operations so that no skill needs to contain inline file manipulation logic.

nodes.label: `scripts/board_resolver.sh`
nodes.description: As a skill or script author, I want a single script that resolves the board path from `project/configs/workflow.json` so that no skill hardcodes `project/board/` or silently uses the wrong path.

nodes.label: Update `/todo` skill to use `todo_manager.sh`
nodes.description: As a skill maintainer, I want `/todo`'s SKILL.md to delegate all `todo.md` file operations to `todo_manager.sh` so that the skill contains no inline shell or file-write logic.

nodes.label: Handoff template for skills invoking `/todo`
nodes.description: As a skill author, I want a structured template asset owned by `/todo` that any skill can populate with pre-collected context and pass to `/todo`, so `/todo` skips questions that have already been answered.

nodes.label: Update `/redo` skill: path bug fix + `/todo` handoff
nodes.description: As a skill maintainer, I want `/redo` to resolve board paths via `board_resolver.sh` (fixing the hardcoded path bug) and to hand off todo creation to the `/todo` skill using the handoff template instead of writing to `todo.md` directly.

nodes.label: Update `/do` skill to use `todo_manager.sh` + `board_resolver.sh`
nodes.description: As a skill maintainer, I want `/do`'s SKILL.md to delegate all `todo.md` operations to `todo_manager.sh` and all board-path resolution to `board_resolver.sh` so the skill contains no inline file ops or hardcoded paths.

nodes.label: Update `/spinoff` skill to use handoff template
nodes.description: As a skill maintainer, I want `/spinoff` to use `skills/todo/assets/todo_handoff_template.md` when invoking `/todo` so that pre-collected context is passed consistently and `/todo` skips questions already answered.

nodes.label: `scripts/todo_cleanup.sh` + session-end hook extension
nodes.description: As a project maintainer, I want a safety-net script that runs on every session end and automatically deletes `project/todo.md` if it is effectively empty, so stale empty files are never left behind regardless of which skill ran.

nodes.label: Jenga Router
nodes.description: Build the local Node.js MCP server (stdio transport) that acts as the central routing brain for the Jenga framework. On startup it scans the `skills/` directory, parses SKILL.md frontmatter (including `keywords` and `examples`), and builds an in-memory skill index. At runtime it exposes MCP tools for prompt routing (`route_prompt`), session management (`active_session`, `end_session`), and skill listing (`list_skills`). Matching uses keyword + lightweight semantic similarity with a configurable confidence threshold (default 0.75). Session state is tracked in-memory and auto-expires on timeout or on receipt of a `[JENGA:SESSION_END:skill_name]` completion signal.

nodes.label: Router Process Bootstrap
nodes.description: As a developer, I want a Node.js stdio MCP server at `mcp/router/` that can be started, stopped, and health-checked so that the rest of the Jenga system has a reliable routing process to connect to.

nodes.label: Skill Discovery & Indexing
nodes.description: As the router, I want to scan the `skills/` directory at startup and build an in-memory index of all available skills so that I can match incoming prompts against them efficiently.

nodes.label: Matching Engine
nodes.description: As the router, I want to match an incoming prompt against the skill index using keyword and lightweight semantic similarity so that I can return the best skill invocation or a passthrough decision.

nodes.label: Session Tracker
nodes.description: As the router, I want to track which skill session is currently active so that subsequent prompts within that session are passed through unmodified until the session ends.

nodes.label: MCP Tool Surface
nodes.description: As a client (hook script or Claude Code), I want the router to expose a complete set of MCP tools so that all routing and session operations are accessible over the stdio MCP protocol.

nodes.label: Intent Classification Model
nodes.description: As the router, I want `mcp/router/matcher.js` to incorporate a local intent/semantic classification model so that prompt categorization goes beyond keyword matching and correctly routes semantically similar but keyword-sparse prompts.

nodes.label: Claude Code Integration
nodes.description: Wire the Jenga Router into Claude Code's native hook system so that prompt routing is completely transparent to the user. A `UserPromptSubmit` hook intercepts every incoming prompt, calls the router, and either passes it through unmodified or rewrites it as a skill invocation (e.g. `/do <original prompt>`). A completion signal protocol defines how skills signal session end, and `jenga init` injects the hook configuration into `settings.json` idempotently.

nodes.label: UserPromptSubmit Hook
nodes.description: As a Claude Code user, I want a `UserPromptSubmit` hook that transparently routes every prompt through the Jenga Router so that skill matching happens automatically without me doing anything special.

nodes.label: Completion Signal Protocol
nodes.description: As the Jenga system, I want skills to emit a structured completion marker when they are done so that the router knows to clear the active session and resume normal matching.

nodes.label: Settings Injection
nodes.description: As a user running `jenga init`, I want the hook configuration to be automatically written into `settings.json` so that I don't have to manually edit any config files.

nodes.label: Jenga CLI
nodes.description: Create the `jenga` command-line tool that users run to configure and operate the Jenga framework. The CLI provides three core commands: `jenga init` (first-time setup wizard that writes `jenga.cli.json` and injects the router hook into the agent's settings), `jenga start` (starts the router as a background daemon), and `jenga status` (shows active session, loaded skills, router uptime). The CLI is packaged via the `bin` field in `package.json` and installable globally via `npm install -g`.

nodes.label: `jenga init`
nodes.description: As a new user, I want to run `jenga init` and be guided through a short wizard so that the Jenga framework is fully configured with no manual file editing.

nodes.label: `jenga start`
nodes.description: As a user, I want to run `jenga start` to launch the Jenga Router as a background daemon so that the hook has a live router to connect to during my Claude Code session.

nodes.label: `jenga status`
nodes.description: As a user, I want to run `jenga status` to see the current state of the Jenga Router so that I can quickly verify the system is running and check what skill session is active.

nodes.label: CLI Entrypoint & Packaging
nodes.description: As a developer, I want the `jenga` command to be installable via npm so that any project using this framework can add it as a dependency or install it globally.

nodes.label: Config & Skill Metadata
nodes.description: Define and enforce the `jenga.cli.json` configuration schema used by the router and CLI, and enrich SKILL.md frontmatter with `keywords` and `examples` fields to improve matching quality. The schema is validated on router startup with clear error messages. Existing skills are updated to include the new frontmatter fields, and the skill template is updated so future skills include them by default.

nodes.label: `jenga.cli.json` Schema
nodes.description: As the router and CLI, I want a validated `jenga.cli.json` config schema so that misconfiguration is caught early with clear error messages rather than silent failures at runtime.

nodes.label: SKILL.md Frontmatter Extension
nodes.description: As the matching engine, I want skills to declare `keywords` and `examples` in their frontmatter so that matching quality is significantly improved over description-only matching.

nodes.label: Multi-Project Router & jenga attach
nodes.description: Fix the single-global-router limitation so each project can run its own scoped router instance, remove the non-functional daemon mode, and introduce a `jenga attach` command that writes the MCP config entry into a project's `.claude/settings.json` so new AI sessions auto-spawn a project-scoped router without manual setup.

nodes.label: Fix jenga attach and permission-level templates clobbering the WorktreeCreate commit-guard hook
nodes.description: As a Jenga framework maintainer, I want `jenga attach` (and any other write path that touches `.claude/settings.json` / `.agents/settings.json`) to preserve the existing `WorktreeCreate` hook configuration, so that running `jenga attach` never silently strips the `install-worktree-commit-guard.sh` invocation and reintroduces the exact worktree-crash data-loss risk that hook exists to prevent.

nodes.label: Multi-Platform Agent Config Parity
nodes.description: The project currently uses Claude-specific variables and hooks (e.g. `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` in `settings.json`, Claude Code hook events like `WorktreeCreate`/`SessionEnd`). This epic makes the configuration layer truly agent-agnostic: Jenga introduces its own canonical env vars and config schema that both Claude and GitHub Copilot (and future agents) can use. Anything achievable via Claude Code integration should be equally achievable via Copilot CLI integration, and vice versa.

nodes.label: Copilot Sub-Agent Delegation Parity
nodes.description: As a developer running the GitHub Copilot CLI on this project, I want Copilot to delegate skill execution to the same named sub-agent (`agents/<agent_name>.md`) that Claude Code would use, so that skills with a `prefered_agent` frontmatter field behave consistently regardless of which CLI is driving the session.

nodes.label: npm Consumer Hook Script Reachability
nodes.description: As a developer maintaining Jenga AI's real npm consumers, I want every hook script shipped via `@jenga-ai/agent` (both Claude Code's `SessionEnd` hook and GitHub Copilot CLI's native `sessionEnd` hook) to correctly resolve its own `lib/` dependencies once installed under `node_modules/`, so that session-end cleanup and project-dir resolution don't silently fail for real downstream consumers.

nodes.label: Workflow Quality & Enforcement
nodes.description: Structural improvements to the agent workflow — format standards, enforcement gates, and quality guardrails that ensure agent-generated board items are consistently structured and that completion statuses are always backed by verifiable evidence, not just mechanical rollup counts.

nodes.label: AC/DoD Enforcement in Agent Workflow
nodes.description: As a developer using the scrum board, I want Acceptance Criteria and Definition of Done to be systematically verified and updated before any story is marked Passed — so that a story's completion status is always backed by evidence, not just task rollup counts.

nodes.label: Reopen Tracking Fields in Board Schema
nodes.description: As a scrum master or developer, I want epic, story, and task files to record when and why a previously completed item was reopened — so that audit trails and history are preserved without polluting the primary date fields.

nodes.label: Dedicated Instructions Location for Task Prerequisites
nodes.description: As a developer or scrum master, I want `_INSTRUCTIONS.md` files (user-action prerequisites) to live in a dedicated `project/instructions/` directory — so that user-facing instruction files are clearly separated from board task files and have a single discoverable home.

nodes.label: Auto-Reconcile on Commit
nodes.description: As a developer using the `/commit` skill, I want the board to be automatically reconciled before any commit is made — so that the scrum board always reflects the true implementation state and no stale or drifted entries are committed alongside the work.

nodes.label: /reconcile-origin Skill — Sync Local Branch with Origin
nodes.description: As a developer, I want a `/reconcile-origin` skill that pulls the latest version of a branch from origin and replays my local changes on top — so that my work is always based on the most recent upstream state without losing any local commits.

nodes.label: Close-Story Skill — Task Closure Metadata & Reporting
nodes.description: As a scrum master or developer, I want a `/close-story` skill that verifies a story's tasks are all in a terminal state, extracts real diff metrics per task, and writes closure metadata to the board — so that story completion is backed by measured evidence instead of manual bookkeeping.

nodes.label: /reconcile Scope Argument — Bounded Epic/Story/Task Reconciliation
nodes.description: As a user of `/reconcile` (directly, or indirectly through `/commit <scope>`'s mandatory reconcile step), I want to append a specific scope or range of scopes (e.g. `E12`, `S03-05`, `E12_S03_T01`) to the invocation — so that a routine sync doesn't re-check parts of the board that were already reconciled multiple times, wasting tokens on a board that currently spans 46 epics / 194 stories / 403 tasks.

nodes.label: Fix the Unsatisfiable Mid-Story DoD Verification Rule in agents/tester.md
nodes.description: As the Tester agent verifying a task partway through a multi-task story, I want a DoD verification rule that distinguishes *"this DoD item is not yet reachable"* from *"this DoD item failed"*, so that I can follow my own contract instead of having to knowingly break it to avoid failing a story that has nothing wrong with it.

nodes.label: README & Documentation Overhaul
nodes.description: Rewrite the README to introduce Jenga AI to first-time adopters — leading with benefits, before/after examples, and a clear getting started path. Create a comprehensive `project/documentation/documentation.md` that documents every skill, agent, and tool with descriptions, usage guidance, and concrete examples.

nodes.label: README Rewrite
nodes.description: As a developer discovering Jenga AI for the first time, I want a README that clearly explains what the framework is, why it exists, and how to get started, so that I can quickly decide whether to adopt it and know exactly what to do first.

nodes.label: Create Documentation Reference
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI user, I want a single comprehensive documentation file that explains every skill, agent, and tool with examples, so that I can find exactly how something works without digging through source files.

nodes.label: Intro Guide & Wiki Structure
nodes.description: As a developer who just finished `/init`, I want a narrative intro guide with linked concept cards so that I understand the philosophy behind Jenga AI and know exactly how to use it effectively from day one.

nodes.label: Agent-Agnostic Documentation Framing
nodes.description: As a developer using GitHub Copilot, Warp, or Codex, I want the Jenga AI documentation to reflect that the framework works with any AI agent or AI-native IDE — not just Claude Code — so that I don't feel excluded before I even try the tool.

nodes.label: /train Skill Enhancement — Production-Grade ML Orchestration
nodes.description:
Evolve the `/train` skill from its current incomplete state (scaffolding + smoke-test only, config flags unimplemented, `training/main.py` never called) into a production-grade ML training orchestrator with full execution lifecycle, experiment tracking, reproducibility guarantees, and AI-guided iteration.

This epic is informed by a deep-dive investigation (Resolve mode) whose output documents are co-located at:
- `project/documentation/plans/train-roadmap.md`
- `project/documentation/plans/scrutiny-train-roadmap.md`
- `project/documentation/plans/solution-assessment-train-roadmap.md`

nodes.label: Foundation — Execution Contract, Config Contract, Full Training Pipeline
Template Manifest Schema + Run Profiles + Observability
Run State Machine + Reproducibility + Metrics Schema
Document that /train is excluded from the public npm package
nodes.description: As a contributor or future maintainer reading `skills/train/SKILL.md`, I want an explicit note that `/train` is intentionally excluded from the public `@jenga-ai/agent` npm package, so that I don't mistake the exclusion for an oversight or accidentally assume it ships to npm consumers.

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph — Application Topology & Data Flow Mapping
nodes.description: Add a per-project knowledge graph as a core Jenga AI framework component. The graph maps application topology (services, modules) and data flows (functions, edges, data types) at two tiers: a human-readable coarse graph (git-tracked JSON) and a queryable fine-grained graph (Kuzu embedded property graph DB). AI agents maintain the graph automatically through a static analysis pipeline, and use it for context injection and impact analysis during task execution. The graph complements existing documentation by tying components and data flows together into a living, machine-readable map of how an application functions.

nodes.label: Schema, Templates & Coarse Graph Foundation
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI developer, I want a standardised schema and templates for the knowledge graph so that all agents produce consistent, validated graph data from day one.

nodes.label: Indexing Pipeline — Static Analysis, Kuzu DB & Git Hook
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI developer, I want an automated indexing pipeline that extracts function-level nodes and edges from source code and stores them in Kuzu, so that the fine-grained graph stays current without manual agent effort.

nodes.label: Agent Integration — Context Injection, Impact Analysis & Summary Frontmatter
nodes.description: As an AI agent, I want to query and update the knowledge graph during normal task execution so that I have richer context about what I am touching and what depends on it.

nodes.label: Lifecycle & Reconciliation — Session-End Hook, Stale Detection & Branch Safety
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI framework, I want the knowledge graph to stay coherent across sessions, branches, and worktrees so that agents never act on dangerously stale or corrupted graph data.

nodes.label: Quality & Measurement — Accuracy Benchmarks, Node Quality Dimensions & Audit Workflow
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI maintainer, I want a measurement framework for the knowledge graph so that extraction accuracy, freshness, and agent task-outcome impact are observable and improvable over time.

nodes.label: DB Migration Job — Export Kuzu to External Database
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI user, I want to be able to migrate my project's knowledge graph from the embedded Kuzu store to an external database so that I can leverage more powerful tooling, shared infrastructure, or persistent cross-session access.

nodes.label: Deferred Extensions — MCP Server, Visualization, Cross-Project & Language Detection
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI framework consumer, I want the knowledge graph to offer richer interfaces and broader coverage beyond the initial JS/TS scope so that it scales to more complex setups and is accessible via standard tooling.

nodes.label: Interactive Architecture Elicitation — Uncharted Integration
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI developer, I want `/uncharted`'s `onboard` and `segment` modes to support a conversational, human-in-the-loop architecture elicitation flow that writes directly to the knowledge graph, so that pre-existing code nobody currently understands can have its architecture captured with human-known intent — complementing E20_S02's prospective AST-diff maintenance rather than duplicating it.

nodes.label: Mechanical Board-to-Graph Populator
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI framework consumer, I want Epics and Stories mechanically synced into `graph.json` as nodes and edges, so that downstream consumers (like the Agent Dashboard's Architecture Map) can read a structured architecture graph without each one re-parsing board markdown for itself.

nodes.label: Clarify Skill (/clearify + /wtf)
nodes.description: Introduce a `/clearify` skill (alias `/wtf`) that lets users signal they don't fully understand something. The skill analyses any attached prompt together with the current conversation, identifies ambiguous formulations, and returns clarifications, simplifications, additional context, and concrete examples.

nodes.label: /publish Skill — Deployment Pipeline Orchestrator
nodes.description:
Introduce a `/publish` skill that guides and executes deployment pipelines from the
current project to remote environments (staging, production, app stores). The skill
is a single entry point with bounded sub-commands, executes pipelines directly where
automation is possible, always confirms before deploying, and surfaces manual steps
where automation is not possible.

Architecture decisions (from deep-dive):
- Single `/publish` skill with sub-commands (`setup`, `deploy`, `history`, `release-notes`)
- Thin orchestrator in SKILL.md; execution logic lives in adapter scripts
- Non-interactive contract is the primary spec; interactive wizard wraps it
- v1 scope: one platform adapter — iOS App Store
- One canonical publish ledger (`publish-history.json`); git tags mirror it
- Mandatory global quality gates + optional per-target gates

nodes.label: Skill scaffold, config schema & non-interactive contract
Droplet adapter — GitHub Actions → SSH deploy
Manual-Steps Adapter Routing Fix — npm/npm-ci/mobile-ios
nodes.description: As a developer running `/publish deploy` against an `npm`, `npm-ci`, or `mobile-ios` target, I want `print_manual_steps()` to show that target's own adapter's manual steps instead of silently falling back to the `mobile-ios` (App Store Connect / TestFlight) steps, so that I'm not misled into following irrelevant post-deploy instructions.

nodes.label: /publish stage — npm Staged Publishing with Pre-Approval Testing
nodes.description: As a maintainer releasing `jenga-agent` to npm, I want a `/publish stage` sub-command that submits a version to npm's staging area, lets me install and smoke-test that exact tarball, and only then approves it for public release — so that a broken release is caught before it is visible to consumers, instead of after, when the only remedies are deprecation or a hasty patch bump.

nodes.label: Human↔Agent Handoff Protocol
nodes.description:
Establish a formal protocol for toggling between agentic and manual development.
When tokens run out mid-task, the agent writes a rolling checkpoint handoff that
the user can follow manually. When the agent resumes, it reads the handoff + the
original task spec to continue from exactly the right point — routing completed
manual work through the Tester as normal.

nodes.label: Handoff document schema & Developer agent rolling checkpoint
/pickup skill — agent resumption after manual work
/doc Document Synthesis Skill
nodes.description: **Goal**: Implement a `/doc` skill that generates or updates documentation files for any target path, with contextual scope inference, multi-source evidence gathering, and board-linked provenance tracking via `last_update` frontmatter.

nodes.label: Board doc provenance schema
nodes.description: Add optional `docs: [...]` annotation support to the scrum board schema so board items can declare which documentation files they affect. `/doc` uses this to resolve `last_update` frontmatter.

nodes.label: /doc skill contract and target resolution
nodes.description: Scaffold the `/doc` skill with argument parsing, the path→objective rule table, and an ambiguity gate that requires user clarification for unknown targets.

nodes.label: Evidence collection and precedence
nodes.description: Collect evidence from all configured sources (user prompt, scrum board, codebase, git history) and enforce a strict precedence chain when sources conflict.

nodes.label: Document synthesis and regeneration
nodes.description: Implement the full-file generation flow. `/doc` owns the entire file — it reads the existing file for context before regenerating. Sections are conditional on scope.

nodes.label: Frontmatter provenance resolution
nodes.description: Resolve `last_update` from completed board items with matching `docs` annotations. Define fallback behavior when provenance is missing.

nodes.label: Integration, distribution, and documentation
nodes.description: Wire `/doc` into the skill discovery and distribution flow, write authoring docs, and validate happy paths and ambiguity cases.

nodes.label: Board Index Substrate — Queryable Library over project/*
nodes.description:
Ship a shell-callable query library that reads `project/*` structural artifacts (epics, stories, tasks, plans, summaries, todo.md, skills, agents) and exposes a small set of graph-shaped queries — `graph::query`, `graph::neighbors`, `graph::orphans`, etc. The substrate is infrastructure: it has **no user-facing slash command in v1**. Its job is to be *imported by other skills* (`/status`, `/impact`, and later `/reconcile`, `/doc-sync`, etc.) so each skill stops re-implementing filesystem traversal against the board.

Deliberately distinct from E20: E20 graphs *application code* topology (services, functions, data flows, Kuzu DB); this epic graphs *board & PM artifacts* over a live filesystem walk. Path-prefix boundary is enforced: this substrate reads only `project/*` and skill/agent frontmatter; E20 reads only code.

**Staged rollout**: only S01 (measurement spike) is queued in `todo.md` at epic creation time. **S02–S07 are gated on S01's measurement result** — if cold-walk latency exceeds 150ms, the persistence-as-optional-cache decision reopens before S02 is decomposed. See `project/documentation/plans/board-index-substrate.md` for the full plan, scrutiny, and solution assessment.

nodes.label: Pre-flight measurement spike — extractor prototype & latency measurement
nodes.description: As the Board Index Substrate epic owner, I want a throwaway extractor prototype that measures real cold-walk latency on the current board and on a synthetic 10× board, so that the persistence decision in the plan doc §7 rests on a number rather than a guess — and so that the remaining stories (S02–S07) can be decomposed with confidence.

nodes.label: Library skeleton & node/edge extraction
nodes.description: As a skill author, I want a shell-callable library at a stable path that walks `project/*` and emits structured node/edge JSON, so that downstream skills (`/status`, `/impact`, `/validate-board`) can stop re-implementing filesystem traversal.

nodes.label: NPM-Compatible Distribution
nodes.description:
Replace the device-local `/distribute` + `.jenga_paths` mechanism with a proper npm publishing workflow. Jenga AI is published as a public npm package (`jenga-agent`) to npmjs.com. Consumer projects install the framework via `npm install jenga-agent`, with a postinstall hook that copies `skills/`, `agents/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/`, and `templates/` into the project root.

Publishing is handled entirely through the existing `/publish` skill, which gains a new `npm` target type alongside the existing `mobile-ios` type. The `/distribute` skill is retired.

nodes.label: Retire /distribute and .jenga_paths
nodes.description: As a framework maintainer, I want to remove the `/distribute` skill and the `.jenga_paths` device-local file so that the codebase no longer contains distribution mechanisms that only work on one machine.

nodes.label: Harden package.json for npm publishing
nodes.description: As a framework maintainer, I want `package.json` to be correctly configured for public npm publishing so that running `npm publish` produces a clean, correctly scoped package that installs framework files into consumer projects.

nodes.label: Refactor publish schema to support multiple target types
nodes.description: As a developer using `/publish`, I want the `publish.json` schema to support both `mobile-ios` and `npm` target types so that a single config file can hold targets of either type without validation errors.

nodes.label: npm adapter and setup wizard
nodes.description: As a developer running `/publish setup --type npm`, I want a guided wizard that collects npm-specific configuration and a well-defined adapter contract so that the framework knows exactly how to publish an npm package for this target.

nodes.label: npm pipeline scripts
nodes.description: As a framework maintainer running `/publish deploy --target npm-registry`, I want dedicated pipeline scripts that validate the environment and execute `npm publish` so that the publish process is automated, repeatable, and safe.

nodes.label: Update existing publish scripts for npm targets
nodes.description: As a developer using `/publish`, I want the existing orchestration scripts to route npm targets correctly so that the full `/publish setup` and `/publish deploy` flows work end-to-end for npm without breaking the existing iOS path.

nodes.label: Update SKILL.md with npm examples and metadata
nodes.description: As a developer reading the `/publish` skill documentation, I want the SKILL.md to include npm target examples and accurate metadata so that I know how to set up and deploy an npm package without reading internal adapter files.

nodes.label: Manifest-Based Delete Reconciliation for Consumer Postinstall Upgrades
nodes.description: As a consumer project maintainer upgrading `@jenga-ai/agent` across a release where skills are renamed, removed, or excluded, I want `postinstall.js` to safely remove only the files *this package's postinstall previously wrote*, so that stale/deprecated skill directories from an older installed version don't linger and keep loading, while my own hand-authored custom skills under `.agents/skills/`/`.claude/skills/` are never touched.

nodes.label: Repo Self-Sync — Restore Root → .claude/.agents Mirror Automation
nodes.description:
Restore the in-repo self-sync automation that E26 dropped. The retired `/distribute` skill's `self_sync()` function (still present in `hooks/distribute-changes.sh`, lines 383–422) mirrored root-level framework directories — `bin/`, `lib/`, `scripts/`, `agents/`, `hooks/`, `mcp/`, `skills/`, `templates/`, `settings.json` — into this repo's own `.agents/` and `.claude/`. That mirror is what Claude Code (and other agents) discover at runtime when working inside the Jenga AI repo. Without it, edits to `/skills/*` in root are invisible to the developer's own session, and drift is already observable (e.g. `.claude/skills/publish/` is running pre-E26 scripts).

E26's `scripts/postinstall.js` is scoped to *consumer* installs (short-circuits when `INIT_CWD === packageRoot`) and copies a smaller set. It cannot double as the in-repo self-sync — this epic fills that gap with a new `/self-sync` skill.

nodes.label: Restore in-repo self-sync as `/self-sync` skill
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI framework developer working inside this repo, I want a `/self-sync` skill that copies root-level framework directories into this repo's own `.claude/` and `.agents/` mirrors, so that my edits to `/skills/*`, `/agents/*`, `/hooks/*`, `/scripts/*`, `/templates/*`, and `settings.json` take effect in my own Claude Code session without me having to run the (now-retired) `/distribute` flow.

nodes.label: self-sync regenerates the root allow-list after mirroring, leaving both mirror copies stale
nodes.description: As a Jenga maintainer, I want a single `self-sync` run to leave all three copies of `lib/skill-allow-list.json` consistent, so that the anti-masquerading allow-list the mirrors ship is never one run behind the source of truth.

nodes.label: Public Mirror — One-Way Private → Public Repo Sync
nodes.description:
This is a private repo, but a public counterpart exists that should receive a curated subset of the same work. Add a `/mirror-public` skill that pushes selected content from this repo to the public repo as a one-way sync — private is always the source of truth, public never merges back.

Distinct from `/publish` (which ships the npm package to npmjs.com) and from `/self-sync` (which mirrors root → in-repo `.claude/.agents/`). This epic is about a *third* distribution surface: the public GitHub repo.

nodes.label: Implement `/mirror-public` skill — one-way private → public sync with blocklist
nodes.description: As a maintainer of this private Jenga AI repo, I want a manual `/mirror-public` skill that pushes a curated subset of this repo (everything except an explicit blocklist) to the public counterpart repo, so that public users see the shippable features without any exposure to private board artifacts, rapports, todos, or logs.

nodes.label: Add feature-inventory and exclusion flags to /mirror-public
nodes.description: As a maintainer of this private repo, I want to preview what ships by category and quickly exclude specific paths, so that I can audit and curate public releases without hand-editing `.publicignore` blind.

nodes.label: Publicignore-Aware Doc-Sync Integrated into /commit
nodes.description: As a maintainer, I want public-shipping features to get flagged for documentation and checked automatically at commit time, so that documentation.md and README.md don't silently drift out of sync with what actually ships.

nodes.label: Harden /mirror-public against destructive overwrites of unmirrored public work
nodes.description: As the maintainer of this private repo, I want `/mirror-public` to prove what it is about to destroy and to refuse to silently break the npm publish contract, so that a `--force` run can never again discard public-side work that was never mirrored back.

nodes.label: Auto-Reconcile Version-Only Drift & Fix Ship-Set Computation
nodes.description: As the maintainer of this private repo, I want `/mirror-public` to automatically absorb version-only drift caused by ordinary `/publish` runs, so that a routine release no longer forces a manual "notice drift → hand-bump private → `--force --yes`" cycle before the next mirror can proceed.

nodes.label: Live npm Registry Verification Gate for /mirror-public
nodes.description: As the maintainer of this private repo, I want `/mirror-public` to verify the package is actually reachable on the live npm registry before it pushes to the public mirror, so that a broken or unreachable published package is never silently mirrored as if the publish state were healthy.

nodes.label: Exclude mcp/router/ and skills/route/ from the public npm package; remove @huggingface/transformers from root package.json
nodes.description: As the maintainer of this private repo, I want `mcp/router/` and `skills/route/` excluded from the public mirror (and therefore from the published npm package), and `@huggingface/transformers` removed from the root `package.json`'s dependencies, so that a plain `npm install @jenga-ai/agent` no longer pulls in the full transformers.js + ONNX runtime + sharp/adm-zip stack (including the unpatched high-severity CVEs already flagged in `package.json`'s own `comments.audit` note) just to serve an optional MCP server most consumers never use.

nodes.label: Fix Private-Skill Leak in Shipped skill-allow-list.json
nodes.description: As the maintainer of the public jenga-npm package, I want `lib/skill-allow-list.json` (which ships in the npm tarball) to only ever list skills that actually exist in the public package, so that private-only tooling names never leak into a public artifact and the `j:` anti-masquerading guard stays correct for public users.

nodes.label: Blocklist Canonical Duplicates of j--Twinned Skills
nodes.description: As the maintainer curating the public mirror, I want `.publicignore` to exclude every canonical skill directory that already has a functional `j-<name>` twin (per `E50_S05`) — except the `jenga`-prefixed skills, which stay public under their canonical name — so the public mirror ships each skill's content exactly once instead of duplicating it under both its bare name and its `j-<name>` alias.

nodes.label: Blocklist j--Twins of Fully-Private Skills
nodes.description: As the maintainer curating the public mirror, I want the `j-<name>` twin directories of the six already-fully-private skills to be blocklisted in `.publicignore` too, so that private-only tooling can't reach the public mirror through its alias directory even though the canonical directory is already blocked.

nodes.label: Rewrite Orphaned j- Twin's Frontmatter Name to j:<name> on Mirror
nodes.description: As a public-package consumer, I want a skill whose canonical directory is blocklisted (so only its `j-<name>` twin ships) to still be invocable via its plain `j:<name>` identifier, so that `E50`'s "every shipped skill is invocable via its `j:`-prefixed name" contract holds on the public package too, without giving up the file-size win `E28_S09`/`E28_S10` already banked.

nodes.label: Make tests/generate-j-alias.bats and tests/init.bats Pass on the Public Mirror
nodes.description: As a maintainer of the public `jenga-npm` mirror, I want `npm test` to pass on a fresh public-repo checkout — not only on the private monorepo — so that the test suite (which ships publicly, unlike `project/board/` etc.) actually validates what a public consumer/CI run will see.

nodes.label: npm Trusted Publishers CI Adapter

The existing `npm` adapter (local `npm publish` + `NPM_TOKEN`) remains untouched — `npm-ci` is a parallel target type for teams that want CI-only publishing with ephemeral tokens and verified provenance badges.

nodes.label: Schema + Adapter Contract

nodes.label: Workflow Generator + Pipeline Script

nodes.label: Strategy Brief Convention
nodes.description: Establish `docs/STRATEGY.md` as a standard Jenga AI project artifact — a strategic brief capturing value proposition, vision, and product boundary (scope). The file targets investors, partners, and the product team doing strategic assessment. This epic defines the canonical format, wires it into the `/doc` synthesis skill as a known target, scaffolds it via `/init` so every new project gets a populated stub, and introduces a `/strategy` interactive skill for guided conversational capture.

nodes.label: STRATEGY.md Format and /doc Target Registration
nodes.description: As a project maintainer, I want `docs/STRATEGY.md` to have a canonical, documented format and be a registered `/doc` target, so that running `/doc docs/STRATEGY.md` produces a well-structured strategy brief and the convention is discoverable by anyone setting up a Jenga AI project.

nodes.label: STRATEGY.md Scaffolding in /init

nodes.label: Config Layer — distribute.config.json and jenga.config.json Schema
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI developer, I want a structured config layer that declares which projects receive distribution and tracks each project's installed version, so that `/distribute` can compare versions, skip up-to-date targets, and maintain an audit trail without relying on a registry.

nodes.label: Distribution Scripts — distribute-changes.sh and commit-version-bump.sh
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI developer, I want battle-tested shell scripts that handle the mechanical work of copying framework files to consuming projects and committing version bumps, so that the SKILL.md orchestration layer can remain high-level and the distribution logic is testable independently.

nodes.label: Skill Orchestration — SKILL.md and Version Lifecycle
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI developer, I want a `/distribute` skill that owns the complete version distribution lifecycle — from selecting release type to reporting results — so that distributing framework updates to consuming projects is a single, safe, guided operation with a dry-run preview before any changes are made.

nodes.label: Register /distribute Skill and Update Documentation
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI developer, I want `/distribute` registered in the skill discovery system and documented in the README, so that the skill is discoverable, usable via the help system, and consistent with how other skills like `/self-sync` and `/mirror-public` are registered.

nodes.label: Project Files Visibility Config Flag (visible / ignored; hidden withdrawn — see follow-up todo)
nodes.description: As a consuming-project owner, I want to control whether Jenga AI's own working files (`project/`, the scrum board, `todo.md`, `queue/`, `rapports/`, etc.) are visible, hidden, or git-ignored in my project, so that the framework's bookkeeping doesn't clutter my repo (or my git history) unless I want it to.

nodes.label: Persist project_files_visibility Across /distribute and Add a Post-Init Toggle
nodes.description: As a consuming-project owner who chose how Jenga AI's working files are tracked, I want that choice to survive framework updates and to be changeable afterwards, so that the setting is a durable project preference rather than a one-shot decision that the next `/distribute` silently discards.

nodes.label: Adaptive Execution Scope for /jenga + /do
nodes.description:
Every task in the Jenga AI workflow currently executes with the same footprint: a dedicated git worktree, a spawned developer subagent, a full plan + summary document pair, and a tester invocation. For a one-line config tweak this is enormously wasteful; for a tightly-coupled group of tasks in the same module it forces the same file to be merged three times.

This epic introduces **adaptive execution scope**. Tasks carry two new frontmatter fields assigned by the scrum-master at breakdown time — `execution_scope` (`task` | `story` | `inline` | `epic`) and `needs_docs` (boolean) — which let `/jenga` and `/do` right-size the execution footprint:

- **`inline`** — tiny self-contained change; implemented in the main session with no worktree, no subagent, no tester. Verified by a per-repository smoke test harness.
- **`story`** — all tasks in a story execute as one bundle: one worktree, one shared developer subagent, sequential per-task execution with a rollback anchor.
- **`task`** — the existing, fully-isolated default.
- **`epic`** — never assigned autonomously; requires `epic_scope_approval: true` set by a human operator.

Because bundles execute multiple tasks in one worktree, the epic also adds the safety machinery that makes that safe: an epic-level bundle lock with a TTL, post-task changed-file extraction, conflict reports when a task touches files it never registered, cross-bundle conflict detection, a close-story pass that compares actual diff stats against the thresholds that justified the scope, and an intent-vs-diff LLM check for `needs_docs: false` tasks.

Settled design decisions (final, not to be re-litigated during implementation):
- All numeric thresholds live in `project/configs/scope-thresholds.json` (`inline_max_files`, `inline_max_lines`, `story_max_files`, `bundle_lock_ttl_minutes`) and are read at runtime by `/jenga` and `/do`. No literal threshold values may be embedded in skill or agent instruction files.
- `threshold_version` must be incremented whenever any threshold value changes, so threshold drift is visible in git history.
- All six new frontmatter fields are **optional**. A task that omits all of them is treated as `execution_scope: task` / `needs_docs: true` and must be processed without error — no agent may reject a legacy board file.
- `epic` scope is never assigned autonomously by the scrum-master. `epic_scope_approval` is set by the human operator only.
- `needs_docs` is assessed independently from `execution_scope`, with one exception: `execution_scope: inline` always implies `needs_docs: false`.
- Every task with `execution_scope` set must carry a `scope_rationale` containing a measurable file-count or line-count claim. Generic rationales are rejected at `/jenga` pre-flight.
- Conflict detection (unregistered files, cross-bundle overlap, scope divergence, intent-vs-diff) is **non-blocking**. It records evidence for later review; it never changes a task's Passed/Failed outcome.

nodes.label: Threshold Configuration
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI maintainer, I want every execution-scope threshold to live in a single versioned config file that `/jenga` and `/do` read at runtime, so that scope decisions are tunable without editing skill instructions and threshold changes are visible in git history.

nodes.label: Task Frontmatter Schema & Validation
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI maintainer, I want the six execution-scope fields formally defined in the board schema and validated at the entry points of `/jenga` and `/do`, so that malformed or unjustified scope assignments are caught before any code is written, while legacy board files continue to work untouched.

nodes.label: Scrum-Master Scope Heuristics
nodes.description: As a scrum-master agent, I want an explicit, threshold-referencing ruleset for assigning `execution_scope`, `needs_docs`, and `scope_rationale` during breakdown, so that scope assignments are consistent, justified by measurable criteria, and never optimistically assigned when tasks contend on the same shared file.

nodes.label: Inline Execution Path
nodes.description: As a developer running `/do`, I want trivial `execution_scope: inline` tasks to be implemented directly in the main session — no worktree, no developer subagent, no tester, no plan or summary docs — verified only by a lightweight smoke test, so that a one-line config change costs seconds rather than a full isolation cycle.

nodes.label: Story-Bundle Execution
nodes.description: As a developer running `/jenga`, I want a story whose tasks are all `execution_scope: story` to execute as a single bundle — one worktree, one shared developer subagent, tasks run sequentially with a rollback anchor — so that tightly-coupled tasks in the same module are implemented in one coherent context instead of being merged into the same file three times.

nodes.label: Close-Story Scope Divergence Detection
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI maintainer, I want `/close-story` to measure what each task actually changed and compare it against the thresholds that justified its assigned scope, so that systematically over-optimistic scope assignments become visible in the data instead of being discovered only when a bundle goes wrong.

nodes.label: Post-Execution Conflict Report
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI maintainer, I want `/do` to record what each bundled task actually touched, flag files a task never registered, and warn when two concurrent bundles expect to touch the same files, so that merge conflicts and silent scope creep inside a shared worktree are surfaced as evidence rather than discovered at merge time.

nodes.label: Epic-Level Bundle Lock
nodes.description: As a developer running parallel work, I want only one story-scope bundle to run per epic at a time, enforced by a TTL-bounded lock file, so that two bundles from the same epic cannot race on the same shared files — while a crashed session can never deadlock the epic permanently.

nodes.label: Intent-vs-Diff Documentation Check
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI maintainer, I want `/do` to LLM-compare a `needs_docs: false` task's stated intent against the files it actually changed, so that skipping the plan-and-summary paper trail does not also mean losing the ability to notice a task quietly expanding beyond what it was asked to do.

nodes.label: Sync /init's Scope-Thresholds Scaffold Template to Live Values
nodes.description: As a user scaffolding a new project with `/init`, I want the seeded `project/configs/scope-thresholds.json` to carry the same threshold values already fixed in this repo's own config, so that new projects don't inherit the binary inline/task cliff that caused the E42_S04 execution-overhead incident.

nodes.label: Introduce the "light" Execution Scope Tier
nodes.description: As a developer running a small-but-not-tiny task through `/do`, I want a `light` execution scope between `inline` and `task` — a single developer pass with self-verification and no worktree or separate tester invocation — so that work too big for `inline` doesn't have to pay for a full worktree+subagent+tester lifecycle it doesn't need (per Finding 2's "Suggested Next Steps" in `project/rapports/analysis/E42_S04-execution-overhead-postmortem.md`).

nodes.label: Tester Trivial-Fix-Path for Mechanical Issues
nodes.description: As a tester finding a clearly mechanical defect (e.g. a missing executable bit, an unreachable dead branch caught by direct exercise of a script), I want to fix it in place rather than filing a full `test_failure` rapport and rework cycle, so that trivial issues don't cost a full rapport, fix commit, re-verification pass, and second mirror sync — the exact pattern that turned a one-line `chmod +x` fix into 3 of the 6 commits recorded in `project/rapports/analysis/E42_S04-execution-overhead-postmortem.md` (Finding 3).

nodes.label: Scrum-Master Task-Folding Rule for Non-Independent Deliverables
nodes.description: As the scrum-master breaking a story down into tasks, I want a standing rule against creating a sibling task for a deliverable that has no independent work of its own, so that a single-line/single-file addition doesn't get its own task ticket that a developer just bundles into another task anyway — as happened with `E42_S04_T02`, created to register `/dev-done` in `CLAUDE.md`'s skill table, then bundled into `E42_S04_T01`'s commit and later deleted once nobody could say what T02 was still supposed to do (Finding 4 of `project/rapports/analysis/E42_S04-execution-overhead-postmortem.md`).

nodes.label: "--trivial" Flag on /todo and /do
nodes.description: As a user who's confident an item is trivial, I want a `--trivial` flag on both `/todo` (at creation) and `/do` (at dispatch), so that I can force `execution_scope: inline` directly instead of waiting on computed thresholds — with the override always logged and a hard fallback to the full pipeline if I'm wrong.

nodes.label: Per-Session Concurrency Cap for Developer/Tester Dispatch
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI maintainer running `/jenga` or `/dooo`, I want a configurable, per-session cap on how many developer and tester subagents can run concurrently, so that a single orchestrating session never oversubscribes the machine/runtime beyond a sustainable number of concurrent agent invocations — while still retrying blocked work automatically as slots free up.

nodes.label: /jenga-permission-level — 5-Tier Permission System
nodes.description:
This repo's `settings.json` currently ships a single fixed `permissions` block (allow-all Bash with a hardcoded deny list). There is no way to temporarily tighten or loosen permissions for a session without hand-editing `settings.json` and remembering to revert it. This epic introduces a 5-tier permission system (`Locked` → `Guarded` → `Standard` → `Elevated` → `Unrestricted`) controlled by a new `/jenga-permission-level [1-5]` command, backed by canonical settings templates, a session-tracking metadata file, a session-start reset safety net, and an opt-in skill-level elevation gate so individual skills can declare a minimum permission level they require.

Settled design decisions (final, not to be re-litigated during implementation):
- `defaultMode` stays `acceptEdits` at **every** level — ~~`autoMode` is never used at any level~~ (previously caused unwanted blocks, e.g. blocking `mirror.sh`). ⚠️ **Partly superseded 2026-08-23 — see Design Revision below.** `defaultMode` still holds; the `autoMode` clause does not.
- Hooks and env vars are identical across all 5 levels — ~~only `permissions.deny`~~ (and never `permissions.allow`, which stays `["Bash(*)"]` at every level) varies. ⚠️ **Partly superseded 2026-08-23 — see Design Revision below.** `autoMode.allow` is now a second varying axis; the hooks/env/`permissions.allow` invariants still hold.
- Level 2 ("Guarded") is conceptually always the default. There is no separate "default_level" config number — to change the *permanent* default, a maintainer edits the Guarded (level 2) template directly. `/jenga-permission-level <n>` only changes the *current session*.
- `sudo *`, `su *`, `dd *`, `mkfs *`, `shred *`, `truncate *` are **never** removed from the deny list at any level, including level 5.
- Skill-level elevation requires **explicit user confirmation** — no silent auto-elevation — and resets back to Guarded **immediately** after the elevated skill finishes (not held until next session start).

nodes.label: Permission Level Templates & Level Matrix
nodes.description: As a Jenga AI maintainer, I want 5 canonical `settings.json` templates representing the Locked/Guarded/Standard/Elevated/Unrestricted permission tiers, plus a documented level matrix, so that `/jenga-permission-level` can deterministically switch session permissions by copying a known-good file instead of computing deny lists at runtime.

nodes.label: /jenga-permission-level Command

nodes.label: Detect classifier-blocked git operations before a gated task burns confirmation cycles
Working-File Path Centralisation — Single Source of Truth for project/ Paths
nodes.description:
Jenga AI already has a path registry. `project/configs/workflow.json` carries a complete `paths` map — `board`, `epics`, `stories`, `tasks`, `rapports_problems`, `rapports_analysis`, `queue`, `scrum_triggers`, `developer_triggers`, `tester_triggers`, `session_handoff`, `logs`, `data`, `configs`, `documentation`, `documentation_plans`, `documentation_summaries`. Almost nothing reads it.

Instead, the literal string `project/...` is hardcoded across the framework. Verified occurrence counts of `project/<subdir>` references at `774d12a`:

| Location | Occurrences |
|---|---|
| `skills/` | 306 |
| `agents/*.md` | 57 |
| `templates/` | 28 |
| `scripts/` | 15 |
| `hooks/` | 5 |

The registry is therefore decorative: the map exists, is maintained, and is ignored. Any feature that needs the working tree to live somewhere other than `./project/` is impossible, and — worse — currently *appears* to work while silently producing wrong results.

nodes.label: Idea Capture Pipeline — /idea Skill & /spinoff Integration
nodes.description:
Introduce a lightweight, "maybe someday" commitment tier below `/todo`: a new `/idea` skill that logs loosely-defined ideas to `project/ideas.md` without any board or promotion overhead. Rewire `/spinoff` — which today saves diverging topics straight to `project/todo.md` — to instead save through `/idea` with a mandatory origin field (the in-progress EST id and a context summary), so mid-task divergences land at the right commitment level and never lose the record of what was interrupted.

This completes the intended design ladder:

```
/idea -> /brainstorm -> /todo or /btw -> /do
             ^
          /spinoff (mandatory-origin, mid-task specialization of /idea)
```

`/idea` itself never gains refine or promotion logic — promoting an idea is simply re-running `/brainstorm` on it, which routes onward through `/btw` or `/todo` as normal. That routing behavior already exists and is out of scope for this epic.

Projects scaffolded before this feature get the file auto-created on first use of the release-note generator, so nothing breaks retroactively.

nodes.label: Inter-Agent Completion Signaling & Worktree Lifecycle Safety
nodes.description:
Three independent incidents have now surfaced the same root cause: the workflow has no single, deterministic, race-free way for one agent or session to know that another is done.

1. `project/ideas.md` / `project/todo.md` — concurrent developer/tester sessions writing `project/queue/.session_handoff.json` (a single shared, single-slot file) can clobber each other; the loser's handoff is silently lost before `on_session_end.sh` ever reads it.
2. A live incident (2026-08-25) — an agent, needing to know when a tester finished verifying a task, wrote an ad-hoc shell polling loop watching a specific commit SHA on a specific branch instead of using the workflow's real completion signal. The condition was unsatisfiable from the start (the tester had committed to `main`, not the branch), and when the worktree was later removed based on `ListAgents` showing the agent as "completed," the orphaned shell loops were invisible to that check — `ListAgents` reports agent lifecycle, not detached OS processes an agent may have left running with their cwd inside the worktree.
3. A diagnosed gap (2026-08-26) — `/jenga` runs as one continuous scrum-master session for the duration of an entire board. Rollup (`scrum_triggers.jsonl`) is only ever drained at "Session Start," so every `story_rollup`/`status_review` trigger written by tester sub-sessions during a `/jenga` run sits unprocessed until some future, unscheduled scrum-master session happens to start. `/do`/`/dooo` only appear reliable by comparison because human-paced usage happens to restart scrum-master sessions often enough to drain the queue incidentally. See `project/rapports/analysis/jenga-rollup-skip-diagnosis-eval.md`.

This epic closes both the specific bugs and the pattern behind them: wherever a story can be enforced deterministically (a script, a git hook, a lock primitive) instead of relying on an agent reading and remembering a written rule, this epic prefers the deterministic mechanism. The one exception is stated explicitly where it applies (see E37_S02_T03) — some fixes are irreducibly instructional and their only backstop is a deterministic fix elsewhere in this epic.

nodes.label: Race-free handoff signal
nodes.description: As an agent in this workflow (scrum-master, developer, or tester) relying on the inter-session handoff queue and the scrum board, I want session handoffs and board-file writes to be structurally race-free, so that two sessions ending close together never silently clobber each other's signal or each other's board update.

nodes.label: Tester Commit Discipline & Signal-Loop Prohibition
nodes.description: As a tester agent verifying a task inside its worktree, I want it to be structurally impossible for my verification commits to land on any branch other than the one I'm verifying, and as any agent in this workflow I want a clearly documented, non-ad-hoc way to wait for another agent's completion, so that a wrong-branch commit or an invented polling loop can never again produce an unsatisfiable wait condition or an orphaned process.

nodes.label: WorktreeRemove liveness precondition
nodes.description: As the workflow removing a task's git worktree once its work is verified, I want removal to check for and refuse to proceed when live processes are still rooted inside that worktree, so that an agent's background watcher (or any other still-running process) is never orphaned by having its working directory deleted out from under it.

nodes.label: In-Run Queue Draining for Long-Lived Orchestrations
nodes.description: As a scrum-master orchestrating a long `/jenga` run, I want the `scrum_triggers.jsonl` queue-processing logic to be invokable mid-session — not exclusively at session start — so that story and epic rollups happen promptly during the run instead of accumulating unprocessed until some unscheduled future scrum-master session.

nodes.label: Reliable Task-Completion Cleanup Across Execution Loops
nodes.description: As a scrum-master orchestrating `/jenga` or another execution loop, I want task-completion cleanup (removing the finished task from `project/todo.md`, tearing the file down when empty, and any equivalent terminal-status housekeeping) to fire automatically whenever a task reaches a terminal status — regardless of which skill dispatched it — so that `todo.md` never goes stale just because a task was dispatched outside `/do`'s own session loop.

nodes.label: Scenario Library & Comparison Playground
nodes.description:
Jenga AI's onboarding docs currently show only single-skill examples and one thin multi-skill sequence in the README. This epic builds a real playground project (a habit tracker, matching the domain already used illustratively in `documentation.md`'s `/pi-plan` example) built twice — once via Jenga AI, once via a raw AI agent session with no framework — to produce a library of real, captured workflow-sequence transcripts illustrating the framework's own "Problem It Solves" claims (session memory, role separation, audit trail, etc.), plus regenerable terminal-cast capture tooling, while fixing a pre-existing documentation drift bug discovered during investigation (`project/documentation/documentation.md` and `project/.wiki/documentation.md` — two copies of the same reference doc that have already diverged).

This epic proceeds through seven stories, in dependency order:
1. **S01** — consolidate the two drifted `documentation.md` copies into one canonical file
2. **S02** — scaffold the habit-tracker playground, built twice, with explicit comparison framing
3. **S03** — run a pilot scenario spike to measure real authoring cost before capping the v1 scenario list
4. **S04** — build a staleness detector so captured scenario transcripts don't silently drift the way the two `documentation.md` copies already did
5. **S05** — build regenerable terminal-cast capture tooling, verified to render across real target surfaces
6. **S06** — cross-link README and the canonical `documentation.md` into the scenario library instead of duplicating content inline
7. **S07** — embed an IBM problem-framing video in the README's "Problem It Solves" section (independent of S01–S06)
