nodes.label: Crucial Flag — Tiered Item-Level Caution & Escalation
nodes.description:
Board items currently carry no signal for "this is high-risk, treat it with extra care." E33's permission-level system tunes caution at the *session* level (what commands can run at all); this epic adds a second, orthogonal axis at the *item* level: a `crucial_level` frontmatter field on stories and tasks that changes how cautiously agents behave on that specific item, regardless of session permission level.

Three tiers, escalating in strictness:
- `advisory` — agents simply raise reporting cadence (more frequent rapport checkpoints); no gate.
- `gated` — agents must get explicit confirmation before specific risky actions (deletes, pushes, credential/secret handling, schema changes) on that item, mirroring the risky-action granularity E33 already applies to `autoMode.allow`.
- `locked` — the item is force-set to `execution_scope: inline` (E32), so it can never be routed to a backgrounded subagent; it can only be worked in the current foreground session, where a live `AskUserQuestion`-style pause-and-confirm is actually possible before every write.

The `locked` tier resolves a real architectural constraint surfaced during brainstorming: a background subagent (spawned via the `Agent` tool, e.g. Developer/Tester under `/do`) runs to completion and cannot pause mid-run to ask the user something — there is no live channel back. Only the current foreground session (the one embodying scrum-master directly, or an inline-executed task) can do that. `gated` and `advisory` don't have this constraint since they don't require a synchronous live pause.

The flag can be set three ways: directly by the user (e.g. via `/todo` or a dedicated command); proposed by scrum-master heuristically during breakdown (e.g. item touches auth/secrets/schema/prod config) but requiring explicit human confirmation before commit, mirroring the `epic_scope_approval` pattern from E32; or requested mid-task by developer/tester via a rapport/trigger escalation — the actual frontmatter write still goes through scrum-master, never the subagent itself.

"Report back to user at will" — the second half of the originating request — is *not* a new synchronous interrupt mechanism (that isn't architecturally available to backgrounded subagents; E37 explicitly prohibits ad-hoc polling as a workaround). Instead it reuses and extends the existing rapport/trigger queue infrastructure (rapports → `on_session_end.sh` → `scrum_triggers.jsonl` → next scrum-master session), which is the framework's actual async "report back" channel today.

nodes.label: Schema — crucial_level, crucial_set_by, crucial_note fields
nodes.description: As a scrum-master agent, I want a standard `crucial_level` field (and provenance fields) on story/task frontmatter so that every agent can consistently read an item's caution tier without inventing ad-hoc conventions per skill.

nodes.label: Flagging paths — direct user set + scrum-master heuristic proposal
nodes.description: As a user, I want to mark a board item crucial myself, and as a scrum-master agent I want to be able to propose a crucial tier during breakdown (subject to explicit user confirmation), so that risk flagging isn't purely manual but also never silently auto-applied.

nodes.label: Per-tier agent behavior — advisory, gated, locked
nodes.description: As a developer/tester agent, I want documented, tier-specific behavior for `crucial_level` so that I handle high-risk items with the right amount of caution without needing item-by-item judgment calls.

nodes.label: Mid-task escalation — developer/tester request crucial_level via queue
nodes.description: As a developer/tester agent, I want a way to flag mid-task that an item turned out riskier than its current `crucial_level` reflects, so that risk discovered during implementation isn't lost until the next full session review — without relying on a synchronous interrupt that doesn't exist for backgrounded subagents.

nodes.label: /uncharted — Investigative Workflow for Foreign & Pre-Existing Code
nodes.description:
Three existing skills investigate things, but none cover "code with no Jenga board provenance": `/deep-dive` investigates *ideas*, not code; `/improve` requires an explicit goal and works on the current codebase toward that goal; `/redo` requires existing board history to rework. Nothing currently helps understand and integrate code that has no board history at all — whether that's a single foreign snippet dropped into the repo, an external source being pulled in, or (the most common real-world case) an entire pre-existing codebase that Jenga AI is being adopted into (`/init` currently has zero handling for this — it always scaffolds fresh).

`/uncharted` introduces a shared investigative engine with three scale modes:
- **`segment`** — a specific file/dir/feature, foreign or already in-repo. Produces an understanding doc plus a normal epic/story/task so the segment gets standard board provenance.
- **`import`** — an external source (URL, pasted snippet, cloned project) not yet in the repo. Pulls it in, then runs `segment` analysis on it.
- **`onboard`** — the whole existing codebase at framework-adoption time. Coarse-first pass (major subsystems, not per-file), produces a capped set of **backfilled** epics tagged `provenance: backfilled` so it's clear they weren't built through Jenga. This mode is **board-level only** — it never restructures or modifies the consumer's actual application code. Jenga's board/skills live alongside the app (`project/`, `skills/`, etc.); the app itself never needs to conform to any Jenga convention.

`onboard` mode hooks into `/init` (detects an existing codebase at scaffold time) and `/reconcile` (detects code with no board linkage during its normal sync pass), in addition to manual invocation.

nodes.label: Shared investigative engine — target resolution & understanding doc
nodes.description: As a scrum-master agent, I want a shared engine that resolves an `/uncharted` target and produces a consistent understanding document, so that `segment`, `import`, and `onboard` modes don't each reinvent analysis logic.

nodes.label: segment mode — analyze and board-integrate a single code segment
nodes.description: As a user, I want to point `/uncharted` at a specific file, directory, or feature that has no board provenance and get it properly integrated into the scrum board, so that unfamiliar or foreign code stops being invisible to the Jenga workflow.

nodes.label: import mode — pull in external source, then run segment analysis

nodes.label: onboard mode — capped, board-only backfill for an existing codebase

nodes.label: Workflow integration — /init hook, /reconcile detection, manual trigger
nodes.description: As a user, I want `/uncharted` to be reachable both explicitly and automatically at the moments it's actually needed, so I don't have to remember it exists.

What this epic controls is everything that makes the package *discoverable* once it's live. Right now, every metadata field that drives discovery is empty or wrong:

- `package.json` has `keywords: []`, `author: ""`, and **no** `repository`, `homepage`, `bugs`, or `engines`
- `description` ("Jenga AI — agentic project management CLI") contains none of the terms the target audience searches for — no "Claude Code", "AI agent", "multi-agent", or "skills"
- The public-facing GitHub repo `samwelmunga/jenga-npm` has an **empty description, zero topics, zero stars, and no homepage**; the richer `samwelmunga/Jenga AI` repo is PRIVATE

This epic fixes the entire in-our-control discovery surface for the already-published **v1.1.0** release.

nodes.label: Maintenance — Framework Hygiene & Schema Drift
nodes.description:
Standing home for small, cross-cutting chore work that does not belong to any feature epic, per the
"use a **Maintenance** epic as the default home for chore tasks" convention in `agents/scrum-master.md`
and `CLAUDE.md`.

Scope is deliberately narrow: one-line-to-one-file corrections that keep the framework's own contracts
self-consistent — schema drift between what an agent or skill writes and what `scripts/validate-board.sh`
accepts, stale cross-references between documents, and similar hygiene. Anything that needs design
discussion, changes a user-facing contract, or spans multiple subsystems belongs in its own epic, not here.

Created 2026-08-26 while processing a `rapport_review` trigger that had no other valid home on the board.

**Reopened 2026-08-30 — E42_S03.** A 149-file repo-wide rename (`JengaAgent` → `Jenga AI`, commit
`c01d0a3`) landed directly on `main` outside the normal Developer/Tester lifecycle — no task ticket,
worktree, or handoff preceded it. File count is well beyond this epic's usual one-line-to-one-file
scale, but the change itself is squarely in scope by kind: a mechanical, no-behavior-change stale-name
correction, and no other epic fits chore-shaped work with no feature owner. See `E42_S03` for the
retroactive record.

`/self-sync`), was added via `/todo`. It's a new skill authorship, not a one-line-to-one-file

nodes.description: As a maintainer running `/jenga`, I want every status value written to a board file to be one the validator accepts, so that `scripts/validate-board.sh` does not report false failures for tasks that are simply in flight.

nodes.description: As a maintainer, I want a rapport to be durable and reported exactly once from the moment it is written, so that the only record of a finding is not lost to a `git clean` and does not arrive as a 23-file dump the first time the session-end hook runs.

nodes.label: Shell Test Harness — Make the Declared bats Suite Real
nodes.description:
`project/configs/test-config.json` declares `bats` as both the unit and the integration framework. The repository contains **zero** `.bats` files. Every shell script in the framework — the `skills/uncharted/scripts/` set, `scripts/`, and `hooks/` — is verified only by a tester agent running it by hand, once, at the moment it was written.

This epic exists rather than a task under `E42 Maintenance` because E42's Purpose scopes it explicitly to "one-line-to-one-file corrections" and states that "anything that needs design discussion, changes a user-facing contract, or spans multiple subsystems belongs in its own epic, not here." A test harness is all three.

**The harness must be designed around a method defect observed on 2026-08-26**, not merely around coverage. During `E40_S04_T03`, two separate findings were raised with confidence and both were wrong in the same way: measured under `discover-subsystems.sh --include-framework` — a flag whose help text reads *"Do not exclude project/ skills/ agents/ hooks/ templates/ .claude/ .agents/"* — and then generalised to the default path that `onboard` actually uses. One was escalated three times as blocking `E40_S04_T04` before a third party re-ran the default path and found the exclusion had been implemented all along.

The lesson is not "write more tests". It is that a suite asserting against *whatever this repository happens to contain today, under whatever flags produced interesting output* would reproduce that defect rather than catch it. Assertions must run against fixture trees with a known expected result, on default flags, and any non-default flag under test must be named in the assertion itself.

A concrete illustration of why the live repo is a poor fixture: a default `onboard` run here yields **9 candidates against a default cap of 8 — exactly one drop**. The drop record is the entire artifact `E40_S04_T03` exists to produce, and this repository exercises it on a single row. A green run against it proves almost nothing.

nodes.label: Execution Control — /break, Stop-the-Line & Scoped Run Status
nodes.description:
Once an orchestration is running, the only way to stop it is to abort it. `/jenga` Phase 4 loops until the board is exhausted with no user interaction by design; `/do` step 8 and `/dooo`'s fan-out loop keep advancing to the next item on their own. Interrupting any of them means killing the turn mid-flight — which can leave a task half-implemented, a worktree orphaned, a bundle manifest without its rollback anchor, or a status write skipped.

What is missing is a **clean stop at a safe boundary**: let the task that is currently running finish and record its status, then halt *before* the next one starts. `/break` provides that. It is deliberately not an in-session interrupt (Esc already does that, unsafely) — it writes a break signal to a flag file that every orchestration loop checks at its task boundary. That indirection is what makes it work for background sub-agents and long `/jenga` runs, where a slash command typed by the user never reaches the running loop.

Two break strengths exist because they answer different needs:
- **Soft (default)** — one-shot. The first loop to reach a boundary consumes the flag, halts, and clears it. The next `/do` or `/jenga` runs normally. This is "let me look at this one thing".
- **Hard (`/break hard`)** — sticky. The flag survives consumption and session end, so every subsequent orchestration refuses to advance until `/break clear` is run. This is "nobody runs the board until I say so".

Appending `status` also prints a progress rapport for the **current scope of execution** — the items this run has dispatched, is running, and has left to go. That is intentionally narrower than `/status`, which prints the entire board regardless of what is in flight.

Per the Skill Implementation Principle, the deterministic parts (writing, checking, consuming, and clearing the flag; resolving and rendering the current execution scope) belong in scripts under `skills/break/scripts/`, not as inline instructions in `SKILL.md`. The loop-side wiring is a one-line script call plus the judgement about what to report to the user.

nodes.label: Interactive Scope Selection for /jenga
nodes.description:
`/jenga` is currently a fully-automated, zero-prompt board orchestrator — it decomposes any unbroken epics/stories, queues every unqueued task, and executes everything it finds with no user interaction. That is the right behavior for CI/scripted callers, but it means a user typing `/jenga` interactively has no way to scope a run to "just this epic" or "just these two tasks" without either editing the board first or letting the whole thing run.

E45 makes `/jenga` interactive by default while preserving the current fully-automated behavior as an explicit escape hatch, via three entry modes:

1. **Bare `/jenga`** — a deterministic script renders a numbered hierarchical checklist of everything on the board. The user selects items by number (comma-separated, mixing levels freely — an epic number plus individual task numbers is valid), then confirms via a full nested Epic > Story > Task tree with counts and checkbox-style toggle/edit support before anything executes.
2. **`/jenga <ids>`** — an explicit comma-separated scope argument bypasses the picker but still shows the same editable confirmation tree before executing. IDs use a fuzzy grammar (2-digit chunking, E/S/T tag detection before or after a chunk, positional fallback for untagged chunks, reject-and-require-disambiguation when a partial ID doesn't uniquely resolve).
3. **`/jenga *`** — the literal wildcard. Skips both the picker and the confirmation step entirely, reproducing today's exact fully-automated, zero-prompt behavior, preserved for CI/scripted callers.

Selecting a parent (epic or story) cascades to only its Pending/eligible descendants (not already-terminal items like Passed or Blocked) and auto-triggers jenga's existing decompose phases (Phase 1/2) for any descendant not yet broken down.

Per this repo's "Scripts Over Inline Logic" principle, all board scanning, ID parsing/resolution, cascade expansion, checklist rendering, and confirmation-tree rendering live in shell scripts under `skills/jenga/scripts/` — never as inline agent instructions. The executing agent's role is limited to gathering raw board items for the scripts, relaying script output to the user verbatim, and forwarding the user's raw reply back into the script.

This epic and its breakdown were fully negotiated turn-by-turn with the user in a `/brainstorm` session; the scope below is committed as-is, not re-decomposed.

nodes.label: Consumer Install Script Path Resolution
nodes.description:
Filed retroactively (per the E42 backfill precedent) after out-of-band diagnosis and a fix executed
directly in-session, ahead of a ticket, at the user's explicit request to unblock an urgent patch
release. This entry exists so the fix has board provenance rather than living only in commit history.

A real consumer reported that `npm install @jenga-ai/agent` followed by `/init` produced only
`.claude/` and `.agents/` (from `postinstall.js`) with no `project/` scaffold, no `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`,
and no git commit — identically on both Claude Code and GitHub Copilot. Investigation found **three**
compounding defects, all in code paths that only ever get exercised by an actual npm consumer — this
monorepo's own dev checkout has a bare `skills/` at its root, which coincidentally masks every one of
these for anyone developing Jenga against itself:

1. **`skills/init/SKILL.md`** instructed running `./scripts/init.sh` (later found to still be wrong even
   as `skills/init/scripts/init.sh`) — a path relative to the project root that only resolves in this
   monorepo checkout. `postinstall.js` mirrors `skills/` and `agents/` only, into `.claude/` and
   `.agents/`; a real consumer has no bare `skills/` at their project root at all.
2. **`skills/init/scripts/init.sh`** itself located `templates/CHANGELOG_TEMPLATE.md` and
   `lib/generate-agent-context.js` via a fixed `$SCRIPT_DIR/../../../` climb. That climb only lands on
   `templates/`/`lib/` when `init.sh` runs from its monorepo location — `postinstall.js` never mirrors
   `templates/` or `lib/` at all (by design; they're meant to be read from `node_modules/@jenga-ai/agent/`
   at runtime), so the same climb from a mirrored copy resolved to nowhere and the scaffold aborted
   mid-run with `set -euo pipefail`.
3. **`lib/generate-agent-context.js`**'s CLI guard compared `process.argv[1]` against
   `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` with strict string equality. Node resolves `import.meta.url` through
   symlinks when loading an ES module; `process.argv[1]` is left exactly as the shell passed it. On
   macOS, `/tmp` and `$TMPDIR` are themselves symlinks into `/private`, so any invocation whose path
   traverses a symlink (an ordinary occurrence — a symlinked home directory, `npm link`, a Docker bind
   mount, a workspace tool) made the two sides disagree and silently skipped `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`
   generation with no error surfaced.

All three are fixed and covered by `tests/init.bats` (new — the bats harness declared in
`project/configs/test-config.json` but never stood up; `E43` remains the epic for building that harness
out properly and generally). Verified end-to-end against a real (non-symlinked) consumer simulation:
`postinstall.js` mirror + a genuine file copy into `node_modules/@jenga-ai/agent/` (not a symlink), full
`init.sh` run, all 12 expected artifacts present including `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, and a real git commit.

**Known residual scope, not fixed here:** the same `../../../`-climb defect pattern (point 2 above)
exists in at least 8 other scripts — `close-story`, `distribute` (x2), `index`, `jenga`, `publish` (x5),
and `uncharted` — found via `grep -rl '\.\./\.\./\.\.' skills/*/scripts/*.sh`. None were exercised or
fixed in this pass; `/init` was the reported, reproducible, user-blocking failure. Tracked as `E46_S02`.

nodes.label: Distributable Project Dashboard
nodes.description:
E05–E09 built a working local dashboard (Express API + Vite/React UI, `project/app/api` + `project/app/ui`) for visualizing board, history, and architecture state — but it was only ever wired up to work against **this monorepo's own** `project/` directory, and `package.json`'s `files` list excludes `project/app/` entirely (confirmed via `npm pack --dry-run`). A consumer who runs `npm install @jenga-ai/agent` has no access to it at all, even though E09's own story titles (`jenga dashboard start`, `jenga dashboard open`) already named it as if it were a real CLI feature. It never became one — `bin/jenga.js` only handles `init`, `start`, `attach`, `status`; the dashboard is only reachable via root `npm run dashboard:start` / `dashboard:open` scripts that shell into `project/app`'s own workspace scripts.

Filed via `/btw` (2026-08-31) after a session that fixed three concrete bugs blocking the dashboard from working at all — a nested-`npm run` flag-forwarding bug (root scripts needed a trailing `--`), a missing `express` dependency (only present under `project/app/api/node_modules`, unreachable from `project/app/ui/scripts/dashboard-start.cjs`), and a route-shadowing bug where the API server's catch-all 404 handler, registered at module-require time, shadowed `--serve-app`'s static/SPA-fallback middleware entirely. All three are fixed and verified in `project/app/api/server.js` and `project/app/ui/scripts/dashboard-start.cjs`. That work made the dashboard functional for this repo; this epic makes it a feature any consuming project gets after `/init`.

This is a generalization/relocation of existing, working code — not a rewrite. The user explicitly scoped it this way ("shouldn't be too much of a pivot").

**E46 precedent to reuse, not repeat:** E46 (Consumer Install Script Path Resolution) found and fixed the exact same defect *pattern* elsewhere in the codebase — scripts that resolve paths via a fixed relative climb (`$SCRIPT_DIR/../../../`) that only lands correctly when running from this monorepo's own checkout, and silently breaks (or resolves to nowhere) once mirrored into a real consumer's `node_modules/@jenga-ai/agent/`. The dashboard's API server almost certainly has the same class of bug today, since it has only ever been run from this repo. E47_S02 should use the same resolution approach E46 landed (fail loudly if no project root is found, don't assume monorepo-relative paths) rather than rediscovering it independently.

nodes.description:
Adds a live, on-demand well-definedness review to the dashboard's Board tab (E06): clicking an AI icon on any epic, story, or task triggers a real-time invocation of a new skill that scores the item 0–10 (integer, no decimals) against a predefined rubric of what a well-defined item should — and should not — contain, and returns concrete improvement suggestions.

Filed via `/brainstorm` (2026-08-31) as one of two pieces of a combined request. The other piece — a collapsible board tree — is scoped as an addendum to the existing, already-`Done` E06 epic (see `E06_S04`) rather than here, since it is a UI fix to a shipped tab, while this is genuinely new capability.

Architecturally, this breaks E05's original "the dashboard API is read-only board parsing" design principle: the new endpoint (`E48_S02`) must shell out to the `claude` CLI and wait synchronously for a structured JSON response, guarded by a startup-generated secret token so that only the dashboard UI (not an arbitrary local process) can trigger a review. This requires an already-authenticated `claude` CLI on the machine running the server — documented as a **known current limitation**, not a permanent architectural lock-in, per the same reasoning applied to E47's own auth/hosting question.

**Blocking dependency on E47 (Distributable Project Dashboard).** This epic assumes the dashboard already resolves data against the consumer's own project (`E47_S02`) rather than this repo's, and assumes the dashboard is running on **port 4305**, renamed from 3001 as part of E47's productization work — no E47 story names a specific port, so that decision is recorded here explicitly rather than being lost. No story in this epic starts before E47 reaches its Definition of Done.

Live review results are persisted back to the reviewed item's own frontmatter (`E48_S03`) so the board can passively show a "last reviewed" state, but every icon click always triggers a fresh live review — the persisted value is for passive display only, never a substitute for re-running the review.

nodes.label: Cross-Agent Context Handoff (resolved_context)
nodes.description:
`project/rapports/analysis/E42_S04-execution-overhead-postmortem.md` (Finding 2) found that the scrum-master's breakdown subagent alone spent ~70,531 tokens re-reading `SCRUM_BOARD_SCHEMA.md`, `skills/lgtm`, `skills/commit`, `skills/self-sync`, and `CLAUDE.md` from scratch — content the orchestrator had already read and resolved minutes earlier — and that the developer and tester subagents each repeated a similar cold start. No mechanism currently shares already-loaded context across an agent-spawn boundary; each subagent independently re-derives what's relevant from source documents its parent already navigated.

This epic extends the existing sender-object handoff contract (already used for scrum-master→developer and developer→tester handoffs, per `CLAUDE.md`) with a `resolved_context` field: a size-capped digest, written by the agent that already did the reading, capturing conclusions already reached (which schema fields are relevant, which skill precedent applies, which decisions are already made) rather than raw file dumps. The digest is delivered via a unique per-task file under `project/queue/context/`, reusing E37_S01's per-session-unique-path pattern rather than a shared, clobber-prone slot. The receiving subagent treats the digest as a starting point it may still verify against source files when needed — never as a restriction on what it's allowed to read.

**Depends on E32.** This epic shares its origin with E32's reopened work (same postmortem) and its digest mechanism is most valuable on the scope-tiered dispatches E32 governs, but the mechanism itself lives at the sender-object/handoff layer used by every agent-to-agent handoff, not just scope-tiered ones — hence its own epic rather than an E32 story, per the `/brainstorm` discussion on 2026-09-01 that produced this epic.

Explicitly out of scope: this epic does **not** revisit the "Resource Budget & Automatic Circuit-Breaker" idea (95%/100% token/time budget with automatic `/break`/cancellation) raised in the same brainstorm — that was considered and dropped in favor of E32's simpler trivial-assessment approach. It also does not propose persistent/long-lived subagent processes reused across tasks — that was explicitly ruled out as conflicting with the worktree-per-task isolation model E37 hardened.

nodes.description: As an agent spawning a subagent (scrum-master dispatching to developer, developer dispatching to tester), I want to pass forward a digest of what I've already resolved from source documents, so that the receiving subagent doesn't have to cold-re-read the same schema/skill/instruction files I already navigated — closing the ~70,531-token redundant-reload gap identified in `project/rapports/analysis/E42_S04-execution-overhead-postmortem.md` (Finding 2).

nodes.label: Skill Namespace Prefix & Anti-Masquerading Allow-List
nodes.description:
Jenga skills are currently invoked as bare `/skill-name` slash commands (e.g. `/status`, `/commit`,
`/init`). Two related risks were raised by the user on 2026-09-02:

1. **Collision risk** — a bare name like `/status` or `/init` is generic enough to collide with a
   skill or command of the same name from another tool, extension, or framework installed in the same
   agent session, making it ambiguous which one actually runs.
2. **Masquerading risk** — with no distinguishing namespace, a malicious or careless third-party skill
   could name itself identically to a Jenga skill (or to a plausible Jenga-sounding name) and get
   invoked in its place, with no signal to the user or the agent that it isn't the genuine article.

This epic namespaces every Jenga skill invocation under a `j:` prefix (e.g. `j:status`, `j:commit`,
`j:init`) and pairs that rename with an allow-list mechanism the agent can check before treating a
`j:`-prefixed invocation as trusted, so the prefix itself can't be trivially spoofed by an unrelated
skill that just adopts the same naming convention.

Origin: raised directly by the user via `/todo` on 2026-09-02, following a `/status` query confirming
no prior board item, deep-dive, or rapport covered this topic.

**Reopened 2026-09-09 — bare-form backward compatibility reversed.** The original DoD decision below
("kept as an alias") shipped as a permanent, never-deprecated guarantee for the old bare `/<name>`
form, with `j-<name>` directory twins (E50_S05) documented as a purely complementary, collision-safety
duplicate — never a replacement. A `/j-error` investigation into a public-mirror stage-deploy gate
failure (`tests/load-playbooks-stepobject.bats`) traced the root cause to `E28_S09`/`E28_S10`
blocklisting 34 canonical bare-name skill directories in `.publicignore`, so the public mirror keeps
only their `j-<name>` twins while `skills/jenga/playbooks/brainstorm-to-mirror.json` still references
those skills by bare name — `load-playbooks.sh` requires every step's `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` to
exist or it silently skips the whole playbook, so the playbook fails to load in the public mirror
(private repo unaffected, since its bare-name dirs were never removed). Rather than patch
`.publicignore` to restore parity with the original policy, the user decided to invert it: bare-name
directories are retired everywhere (private repo included), `j-<name>` is promoted from twin to the
sole canonical form, and the bare `/<name>` form hard-breaks once its directory is deleted — no
redirect/deprecation shim. This session amended this epic rather than opening a new one, since it
reverses rather than extends the original DoD decision. Story breakdown for this reopening is left to
`/jenga`'s decomposition pass.

nodes.description: As a Jenga framework maintainer, I want the post-reversal skill-naming contract written down and ratified before any directory is touched, so that the eight downstream stories in this reopening all implement against one unambiguous target state instead of each re-deciding it.

nodes.label: Repoint Every Functional Bare Skill-Path Reference to Its Twin
nodes.description: As a Jenga framework maintainer, I want every executable reference of the form `skills/<bare>/...` rewritten to `skills/j-<bare>/...` **while both directories still exist**, so that the later deletion of the 40 bare directories cannot break a single code path mid-sequence.

nodes.label: Resolver, Allow-List & Router Cutover to the Twin Directory
nodes.description: As a Jenga framework maintainer, I want every component that *resolves* or *trusts* a skill identifier to work in a twin-only world before the bare directories disappear, so that the anti-masquerading allow-list and the NL router keep functioning across the cutover rather than silently failing open or dropping skills.

nodes.label: Playbook Step-Name & Loader Cutover
nodes.description: As a Jenga user running a multi-skill playbook, I want playbook `steps` to name skills by their canonical twin directory, so that `brainstorm-to-mirror` loads in the public mirror instead of being silently skipped — the exact failure that reopened this epic.

nodes.label: Retire or Invert the Twin-Generation Scripts
nodes.description: As a Jenga framework maintainer, I want the bare-name→twin generation relationship resolved before the bare directories are deleted, so that the tooling which currently *requires* a bare source directory does not become a hard-failing dead end the moment its input disappears.

nodes.label: Delete the 40 Bare-Name Skill Directories
nodes.description: As a Jenga framework maintainer, I want the 40 canonical bare-name skill directories removed from the private repo and both generated mirrors, so that `j-<name>` becomes the sole canonical directory everywhere and the private/public split that caused the stage-deploy failure cannot reoccur.

nodes.label: Distribution-Surface Cleanup — .publicignore, Mirror Orphan Rewrite & Consumer Reconciliation
nodes.description: As a Jenga maintainer publishing to the public mirror and to npm consumers, I want the distribution machinery updated for a twin-only tree, so that the public mirror stops compensating for a private/public split that no longer exists and existing consumers cleanly shed their orphaned bare directories.

nodes.label: User-Facing Docs, Templates & Agent-Context Cutover
nodes.description: As a Jenga user or a downstream agent reading generated context, I want every user-facing document and generated template to describe the sole-canonical-form policy, so that nothing still promises me a bare `/<name>` command that no longer exists.

nodes.label: Cutover Verification Gate & Epic DoD Closure
nodes.description: As a Jenga maintainer, I want a single end-to-end gate that proves the sole-canonical-form cutover is complete and correct across every surface, so that E50's reopened Definition of Done can be closed on evidence rather than on the assumption that eight stories each did their part.

nodes.label: Twin Content-Divergence Audit & Back-Fill Before Bare-Name Deletion
nodes.description: As a maintainer shipping fixes to the public mirror, I want every `skills/j-<name>/` twin to carry the full content of its bare-name source before those sources are deleted, so that merged fixes actually reach consumers instead of being silently stranded in a directory the mirror never ships.

nodes.label: Public-Safe Playbook Coverage & Visibly-Skipped Private Tests
nodes.description: As a public-mirror consumer, I want at least one playbook I can actually run and a test suite that tells me when coverage was withheld, so that the playbooks feature is usable downstream and its gaps are visible rather than silent.

nodes.label: Ticket Lifecycle Status Automation (Merged / Publicized / Privatized / Deployed to Stage / Deployed to Prod)
nodes.description:
Extend the board status vocabulary with five new, deterministically script-set statuses that track a ticket's journey after it's closed: `Merged` (mirrored into `.claude/`/`.agents/` via `/self-sync`), `Publicized` (shipped to the public `jenga-npm` mirror via `/mirror-public`), `Privatized` (permanently excluded from the public mirror via `.publicignore`), and `Deployed to Stage` / `Deployed to Prod` (published via the npm-ci target's stage/prod jobs, reported back from the public repo's CI). None of these are agent-judged — each is set by a script reacting to a concrete, checkable event (a sync/mirror run's file diff, a static blocklist membership check, or a public-repo git tag), never by developer/tester/scrum-master discretion.

Filed via `/spinoff` → `/idea` → `/brainstorm` (2026-09-02), originating from a clarifying question during the `E06_S05` (Board Tab kanban-column) `/todo` session.

nodes.label: Schema & Status Vocabulary
nodes.description: As a scrum-master (and any script that reads or writes board status), I want `Merged`, `Publicized`, `Privatized`, `Deployed to Stage`, and `Deployed to Prod` recognized as valid statuses so that later automation (E51_S02–E51_S05) can write them without failing board validation.

nodes.label: "Merged" Status via /self-sync
nodes.description: As a developer relying on the board to reflect reality, I want tickets automatically marked `Merged` once their work is mirrored into `.claude/`/`.agents/`, so the board shows what's actually live in this session's tooling without a manual status update.

nodes.label: "Publicized" and "Privatized" Status via /mirror-public
nodes.description: As a developer, I want tickets automatically marked `Publicized` when their work ships to the public mirror, or `Privatized` when their work is permanently excluded from it, so the board distinguishes "will never go public" from "hasn't gone public yet."

nodes.label: Public-Repo CI Tagging on Stage/Prod Success
nodes.description: As a maintainer, I want the public `jenga-npm` repo's own CI to tag its own commit on a successful stage or prod publish, so there's a durable, public record of what shipped and when — without granting that CI any write access back into the private repo.

nodes.label: "Deployed to Stage" / "Deployed to Prod" Consumption
nodes.description: As a developer, I want the private repo's board to reflect what the public repo's tags say has shipped, so `Deployed to Stage`/`Deployed to Prod` status is kept current without any cross-repo write access.

nodes.label: Revise E06_S05's Kanban Columns for the Five New Statuses
nodes.description: As a dashboard user, I want the Board tab's kanban columns to reflect the real post-close lifecycle (`Merged`, `Publicized`/`Privatized`, `Deployed to Stage`/`Deployed to Prod`), not a single placeholder "Deployed" column, so the board view stays accurate once this epic ships.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md and the board schema contradict each other on who may write Merged
nodes.description: As a Jenga agent deciding whether a status write is legitimate, I want one unambiguous rule about who may write lifecycle statuses, so that a script doing exactly what its epic designed it to do doesn't read as a governance violation.

nodes.label: Agent Orchestration — Cross-Session Message Isolation
nodes.description:
On 2026-09-05, while working `E28_S11` (a `crucial_level: gated` task touching the
`/mirror-public` push path), a confirmation message meant for this session's own paused tester
subagent — approving a throwaway local-only rehearsal for task `E28_S11_T01` — was instead
delivered to a different, unrelated tester session (`tester-1788622344-e51s04t02`), which was
independently waiting on its own separate gated confirmation for an unrelated task, `E51_S04_T02`.
That session then acted on the misdirected approval: it ran its own rehearsal and committed a
rapport file (`430a0c0`) directly to this repo's shared `main` branch, without this session's user
ever having reviewed or approved that specific action in this conversation.

The concrete harm this one time was minimal (a single new rapport markdown file, no code change, no
push to any remote) — but the mechanism is the concerning part. The entire point of `crucial_level:
gated` is that a human confirms *this specific action*; if a confirmation intended for one gated
request can be silently redirected to a completely different pending gated request in a different
session, that safety property is not actually being enforced the way the schema documents it.

This epic exists to investigate the routing/isolation behavior of backgrounded subagent messaging
(`Agent`/`SendMessage` continuation) in this environment, determine whether anything on the Jenga
side can detect, prevent, or at least loudly surface this kind of cross-talk, and decide what (if
anything) is actually fixable versus an accepted limitation of the underlying harness.

Origin: raised directly by the user on 2026-09-05, immediately after the incident was discovered
and transparently disclosed mid-session during `E28_S11`'s execution.

nodes.label: [SPIKE] Investigate 2026-09-05 Cross-Session Gated-Confirmation Misroute
nodes.description: As the maintainer of this framework, I want a clear-eyed investigation of the 2026-09-05 cross-session message misroute (recounted in `E52`'s Purpose section) — what actually happened, what could be verified from inside this repo, and what if anything is fixable — so that a future occurrence is recognized quickly instead of re-investigated from zero, and so we know whether a concrete mitigation is worth building.

nodes.label: Jenga Natural-Language Dispatcher & Playbooks
nodes.description:
Let `/jenga` (frontmatter `j.jenga`) accept free-text intent as its single
argument, in addition to its existing bare / `<ids>` / `*` forms, and either
route that intent to the best-matching skill or propose an ordered
multi-skill workflow — instead of requiring the user to know all ~82
individual command names.

`/jenga` already defines three argument shapes (bare, `<ids>`, `*`), so any
argument that is neither an ID pattern nor the literal `*` is unambiguously
natural language — that argument shape is itself the trigger for this
branch. No new sigil or trigger prefix is introduced.

`skills/route/SKILL.md` already implements natural-language → single-skill
matching with board and documentation enrichment. That matching logic is
**absorbed and reused, not duplicated**, by `/jenga`'s new branch. The
genuinely new capability this epic adds is **chained multi-skill
playbooks** (e.g. `brainstorm -> j.todo -> j.do -> j.dev-done ->
j.mirror-public`), which `/route` cannot do today.

The skill catalog used for matching must be generated (reusing
`lib/generate-skill-allow-list.js`'s existing inventory output) rather than
hand-maintained, so the matcher can never drift out of sync with the real
skill set.

nodes.label: Absorb /route's NL Skill Matching into /jenga's Fallback Branch
nodes.description: As a user, I want `/jenga` to route free-text intent to the best-matching skill so that I don't need to know exact command names or separately invoke `/route`.

nodes.label: Multi-Skill Playbook Proposals for Cross-Cutting Intent
nodes.description: As a user, I want `/jenga` to propose an ordered chain of skills when my free-text intent spans more than one, so that I don't have to manually invoke each step of a workflow myself.

nodes.label: Playbook Type Registry, StepObject Schema, and Load-Time Validation
nodes.description: As a playbook author, I want playbook steps to carry typed parameters (`skill`/`playbook`/ `instruction`/`forward_from`/`resolve`) validated against a shared type vocabulary at load time, so that a malformed or type-incompatible step is caught before a chain ever runs, not mid-chain.

nodes.label: Conditional Step Execution and the `skipped` Status
nodes.description: As a playbook author, I want a step to be conditionally skipped based on a prior step's typed output, so that a chain can branch without the user having to hand-edit which steps run each time.

nodes.label: Playbook-to-Playbook Composition
nodes.description: As a playbook author, I want a playbook to include another playbook as one of its steps, so that I can compose small, reusable chains into larger ones instead of duplicating steps across files.

nodes.label: `resolve` Transform, Failure Handling, and Direct Invocation (`j.playbook <id>`)
nodes.description: As a playbook author, I want a `resolve` step to reshape or filter a forwarded value between two steps, and as a user I want a way to invoke a specific playbook directly by ID, so that playbooks can bridge mismatched types without silently breaking and I don't have to phrase a matching prompt to reach a playbook I already know by name.

nodes.label: Confirmation-Driven `resolve` (Deferred, Safety-Gated)
nodes.description: As a playbook author, I want the option for a `resolve` step to eventually pre-answer a downstream confirmation gate on the user's behalf, so that a fully-vetted, trusted chain doesn't stop for a confirmation whose answer is already implied by upstream data — but only once this capability has been through a dedicated safety review, since it directly touches Jenga's interactive-by-default human-in-the-loop model.

nodes.label: Document the Playbook Output-Type System for End Users
nodes.description: As a Jenga user reading the docs (not the skill-authoring guide), I want to understand what the `output_types` type system is and see it reflected per-skill in the reference documentation, so I don't have to read `docs/skill-authoring.md` (a contributor-facing doc) to find out a skill I'm about to use in a playbook produces a `text`/`id_list`/`file_list` value.

nodes.label: Built-State & Scenario Test Harness for Skills, Scripts, and Templates
nodes.description:
The existing test suite (`tests/*.bats`, run via `npm test`) validates individual scripts and
fixtures in isolation, but nothing verifies that every skill, script, and template is actually
**accessible and functional once built** — i.e. after `/self-sync` mirrors root `skills/`,
`agents/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/`, `templates/` into `.agents/`/`.claude/`, or after `/mirror-public`
produces the public npm package. A file present in the source of truth but silently dropped,
malformed, or broken in a mirror (as already happened once — see `E28_S12`'s public-mirror parity
regression) currently goes undetected until a real consumer hits it.

Separately, the existing bats suite is entirely unit/fixture-level — it never exercises a
realistic multi-step user flow (e.g. `/todo` → `/do` → `/commit`) the way Playwright or Cypress
exercise a real UI flow. A regression in how skills compose (arguments passed between commands,
frontmatter contracts, playbook chaining once `E53` ships) has no coverage today.

This epic adds two complementary layers:
1. **Built-state accessibility dry run** — deterministic script logic that walks every skill,
   script, and template in a given built state (`.agents/`, `.claude/`, or a public-mirror
   worktree) and confirms it is present, has valid frontmatter/shebang, and is
   invocable/parseable — without executing its real side effects (`E54_S01`).
2. **Scenario / mock-flow runner** — fixture-driven "mock flows" that simulate a sequence of
   skill invocations against a scratch project directory (mirroring this repo's existing bats
   fixture convention) and assert on the resulting board/file state, catching cross-skill
   regressions that unit tests miss (`E54_S02`).

**On the "type" system (E53_S03):** `E53_S03`'s playbook type registry (`output_types`,
`StepObject`) is still `Pending` and unrelated in scope (it types playbook step data, not test
scenarios). This epic defines its own lightweight scenario/fixture schema now rather than
blocking on it. If, once `E53_S03` ships, its type vocabulary turns out to be a good fit for
describing scenario inputs/outputs, adopting it is a future enhancement to `E54_S02` — not a
dependency of this epic.

nodes.label: Built-State Accessibility Dry Run
nodes.description: As a maintainer, I want an automated dry-run check that confirms every skill, script, and template is present and structurally valid across all of this repo's built states (`.agents/`, `.claude/`, and the public-mirror worktree), so that mirror/copy regressions are caught before a real consumer hits them.

nodes.label: Scenario / Mock-Flow Test Runner
nodes.description: As a maintainer, I want Playwright/Cypress-style scenario tests that simulate a short chain of real skill invocations against a scratch project directory and assert on the resulting file/board state, so that regressions in how skills compose (arguments passed between commands, frontmatter contracts) are caught by CI instead of by a user mid-flow.

nodes.label: Merge-to-Main Guardrail for Completed Tasks
nodes.description:
Today, nothing structurally guarantees that a task's worktree branch ever lands on `main` once it
reaches `Passed`. `agents/developer.md`'s Worktree Management section says only "merge and remove
the worktree when work is complete" — a one-line instruction with no concrete mechanism behind it.
`skills/commit/SKILL.md`'s normal-mode flow (reconcile → doc-sync → prerequisite check → commit →
next-epic check) has no merge step at all, and `agents/tester.md` explicitly forbids the tester
from committing to `main`. A task can therefore sit `Passed` indefinitely with its actual work
stranded on an unmerged branch.

Worse, the one existing safety net — `/reconcile`'s Phase 2 implementation check — has a blind
spot that hides exactly this failure mode: it runs `git log --all --oneline --grep="<task_id>"`
(`skills/reconcile/SKILL.md` line 105), and `--all` scans every ref including unmerged local
branches. Because every commit convention mandates embedding the task ID in the message, this
check reliably finds the commit on its own orphaned branch and reports "implementation confirmed —
no action needed," even though the work never reached `main`. `/reconcile`'s actual
merge-orphaned-branch prompt only fires when that grep *fails*, which it won't for a properly
tagged, unmerged commit — so a long-sitting `Passed`-but-unmerged task is invisible to the one tool
meant to catch board/reality drift.

This epic closes that gap in two steps, per the user's explicit choice of a detection-first, then
hard-gate approach (auto-merging to `main` unattended was considered and rejected as too high
blast-radius for a first pass):

1. **Fix the detection blind spot** (`E55_S01`) — `/reconcile`'s check must distinguish "a commit
   exists somewhere" from "a commit is actually reachable from `main`," so it correctly flags
   `Passed`-but-unmerged tasks instead of false-confirming them.
2. **Hard-gate story closure on verified merge state** (`E55_S02`) — `skills/close-story/scripts/check-story-closeable.sh`
   currently verifies only that every task is in a *terminal status* (`Passed`/`Done`). It must
   additionally verify each task's recorded commit(s) are reachable from `main` before the story
   can close — turning "finished but unmerged" into a structural block on rollup, not just a
   report someone might ignore.

nodes.label: Hard-Gate Story Closure on Verified Merge State
Story-Level Branch Isolation
nodes.description:
Generalizes `E32_S05`'s existing all-story-scope bundle mechanism (one shared worktree, sequential
task execution, rollback anchor — but gated behind "every task in the story is
`execution_scope: story`") into a predictable, named **story branch** that every story with at
least one `task`/`story`/`epic`-scope task gets — mixed-scope stories included. `E32_S05`'s shared
bundle worktree becomes *the* story branch rather than a parallel concept.

Today, each task branches its own worktree straight off `main` (`agents/developer.md`'s
`<E##_S##_T##-slug>` convention) and — per this session's `E55` investigation — nothing
structurally merges that work back into `main` at all. This epic replaces that flat model with a
two-level one: task work merges up into its story's branch, and the story branch merges down into
`main` only once, at story close, after every task in the story is terminal.

**Supersedes `E55` (Merge-to-Main Guardrail for Completed Tasks).** `E55` was scoped around
tasks merging (or failing to merge) directly into `main`. Under this model that target is wrong —
tasks merge into the *story branch*, and only the story branch ever merges into `main`. Rather than
retrofit `E55`'s two stories, its intent is carried forward here, reworked against the correct
target: `E56_S05` (reconcile reachability) is `E55_S01` reworked, and `E56_S04` (story-close merge
+ hard gate) is `E55_S02` reworked plus the actual merge action `E55_S02` never had. `E55`'s epic
and both stories are marked `Rejected` with a pointer to this epic — see each file's own note.

Locked design decisions from the `/brainstorm` session that produced this epic:
- **Branch existence is conditional on story composition.** A story branch is created lazily, off
  `main`, the first time that story gets a `task`/`story`/`epic`-scope task queued. A story made up
  entirely of `inline`/`light` tasks never gets a branch — its work continues straight to `main`,
  unchanged from today.
- **No split-brain once a branch exists.** Once a story has a branch, *all* of that story's work
  targets it — including any `inline`/`light` tasks in the same story, which still skip the
  worktree step but commit directly onto the story branch (via git plumbing, not a checkout swap —
  see `E56_S03`) rather than bypassing to `main`.
- **No locking.** A story-branch ref update is a compare-and-swap (`git update-ref <branch> <new>
  <old-tip>`); a race is rejected atomically by git itself. No flag file, no retry loop — a
  rejected update fails and reports.
- **One conflict policy for both merge levels (hybrid).** Task→story-branch and
  story-branch→`main` merges both: auto-attempt resolution in a third worktree up to 3 times, then
  escalate to a **gated human confirmation** on the final attempt (replacing today's silent
  `Blocked` + rapport with no merge action at all).
- **Naming matches existing precedent, kebab-case.** Story branches are named
  `e##-s##-slug` — the same casing family as `agents/developer.md`'s existing
  `<E##_S##_T##-slug>` task-branch convention. Task branch names are unchanged; only what they
  branch **from** changes (the story branch, not `main`).

nodes.label: Story Branch Lifecycle
nodes.description: As a developer running `/do` or `/jenga`, I want a story with any `task`/`story`/`epic`-scope work to automatically get a predictably-named branch off `main`, so that its tasks have a stable, shared home to merge into instead of each landing independently on `main`.

nodes.label: Task Merge-Up Into Story Branch
nodes.description: As a developer, I want a completed task's worktree branch to merge into its story's branch instead of `main`, with a defined conflict-resolution policy, so that "finished" task work reliably lands somewhere real instead of relying on an unenforced "merge when done" instruction.

nodes.label: Inline/Light Direct-to-Story-Branch Commit Path
nodes.description: As a developer executing an `inline`/`light` task inside a branched story, I want that task's commit to land on the story branch without a worktree and without disturbing the session's own checkout, so that a story never ends up with some of its work on the branch and some on `main`.

nodes.label: Story-Branch-to-Main Merge at Story Close
nodes.description: As a maintainer, I want `/close-story` to actually merge a story's branch into `main` once every task is terminal — not just check status — so that a "closed" story reliably lands its full body of work on `main` rather than leaving it stranded on a branch nobody merges.

nodes.label: Reconcile Reachability Retargeting
nodes.description: As a maintainer, I want `/reconcile`'s implementation check to verify a task's commit is reachable from its **story branch** (not `main`), plus a separate check that the story branch itself is reachable from `main` once a story claims to be closed, so that drift detection matches this epic's two-level branch model instead of false-confirming work that never left a branch.

nodes.label: Train Skill Deprecation & Package Extraction
nodes.description:
Disable and deprecate the `/train` skill in both the private repo and the public mirror, while
**preserving** its implementation intact so it can be moved to its own package later. Deprecation
here means "stop offering it as a Jenga skill", not "delete it" — the extraction is the point, and
anything that destroys the payload defeats the purpose.

Captured via `/btw` on 2026-09-10 by direct user instruction.

nodes.label: Disable /train and Surface a Deprecation Notice Everywhere It Resolves
nodes.description: As a Jenga user who reaches for `/train`, I want a clear notice that the skill is deprecated and moving to its own package, so that I stop depending on it without wondering whether it broke.

nodes.label: Preserve the Extraction Payload and Document the Future Package Boundary
nodes.description: As the maintainer who will later publish `/train` as its own package, I want its full payload and boundary written down now, so that the extraction is a move rather than an archaeology exercise.
